By examining seven key task domains—knowledge anchoring, prediction, assessment, intelligent design and simulation, data augmentation, embodied intelligence, and decision support—we show how LLMs and AI agents can reshape traditional disaster-resilience workflows through enhanced multimodal perception, long-horizon reasoning, cross-stage coordination, and automated task execution. Two representative case studies further demonstrate the feasibility of this paradigm: (1) a multimodal building-damage assessment system capable of city-scale semantic reasoning and transparent diagnostic interpretation, and (2) a LangGraph-based reasoning agent for automated seismic resilience assessment and recovery decision-making of infrastructure systems. These cases highlight the potential of LLMs and AI agents to bridge fragmented data sources, orchestrate multi-stage analytical workflows, and support high-impact resilience applications. Despite these advances, key challenges remain, including data scarcity, reliability and consistency issues, deployment constraints, and ethical or security concerns. Addressing these limitations is essential for developing trustworthy, efficient, and scalable intelligent disaster-prevention systems. Overall, this work establishes a unified cognitive–action paradigm that offers forward-looking pathways for the next generation of intelligent and resilient infrastructure technologies.

title: A resilient location of urban fire stations considering multiple-path characteristic of uncertain road networks: Framework and case study
Invulnerability analysis of metro-bus double-layer network considering passenger flow transfer through inter-layer edges: Methodology and management strategies
Path integral solution of the Li-Chen equation and its application to global dynamic reliability via time-variant extreme process
A reliability analysis method considering variable updates under multiple progressive damage coupling
Re-examining the explanatory boundaries of car-following models through fitting errors decomposition to uncover adaptive feedback
Dynamic human reliability and dual-type quality prediction in human-machine collaborative tuning manufacturing systems
Multivariate degradation modeling with long-term dependency for operational reliability assessment
New approximations for the renewal function of the Weibull distribution
Meta-predictive maintenance for rapid adaptation across diverse infrastructure maintenance tasks
Multi-objective optimization of network disintegration via deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Network disintegration problems, such as halting the spread in epidemic networks and disrupting the network structures of criminal syndicates, have attracted increased attention from many complex network researchers in recent years. Existing network disintegration strategies predominantly adopt a single-objective optimization framework that focuses solely on network function destruction, but neglects critical secondary objectives such as cost minimization. This work aims to solve the multi-objective network disintegration (MND) problem by maximizing the weakened network functionality while minimizing the disintegration cost to develop a more practical model. To this end, we propose the DRL-MND framework, which leverages deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to tackle the MND problem. The DRL-MND decomposes the MND problem into scalar subproblems, each solved by a designed neural network model. A neighborhood-based parameter transfer strategy is then incorporated into Actor-Critic training algorithms to enable coordinated optimization of the subproblem model parameters. Experimental results validate that the proposed method outperforms conventional multi-objective optimization algorithms in terms of effectiveness and competitiveness. The DRL-MND exhibits novel characteristics, including fast solution speeds and strong generalization capabilities.

title: AI-augmented modeling of post-fire soil hydraulic conductivity across environmental gradients for geohazard assessment
abstract: Wildfires substantially alter soil hydraulic and mechanical properties, reshaping infiltration dynamics and increasing susceptibility to rainfall-triggered geohazards such as debris flows and landslides. A key challenge is the scarcity of paired pre- and post-wildfire soil hydraulic conductivity measurements across vegetation types, soil textures, and burn severities. The main objective of this study is to use generative AI algorithms, together with a curated dataset of measured pre- and post-fire soil hydraulic properties, to augment sparse observations and produce realistic synthetic conductivity pairs across diverse environmental gradients. A curated cross-site dataset of 46 paired conductivity measurements was compiled, and six tabular generators, Gaussian Copula, GAN, VAE, Copula+GAN, VAE+GAN, and a Mixture of Experts (MoE), were trained to produce synthetic conductivity tables conditioned on soil, vegetation, and burn severity. Model performance was evaluated using distributional fidelity metrics, rare-group behavior, memorization diagnostics, and Train-on-Synthetic/Test-on-Real (TSTR) utility. Scale effects were also assessed by varying synthetic sample sizes, and synthetic conductivity contrasts were propagated through a slope stability model to evaluate downstream geotechnical implications. Results show that VAE, VAE+GAN, and MoE provide the strongest balance of fidelity and predictive utility (normalized MAE within 5 to 10% of the real-data baseline) while maintaining low memorization risk (MI ≈ 0.40 to 0.52, versus >0.8 for copula-based baselines). Synthetic datasets enlarged to approximately three to six times the real sample size stabilize dependence structures and improve downstream accuracy. In slope-stability propagation, GAN and MoE most closely reproduced reference factor-of-safety distributions, whereas VAE slightly smoothed lower tails.

title: The logistic-additive Weibull distribution with statistical properties and regression modeling for reliability applications
Revisiting the cross entropy method for first-passage probability of Gaussian-process excited uncertain linear structural dynamic systems
abstract: This study presents a specialized Monte Carlo method for the reliability assessment of linear structural systems subjected to Gaussian process excitations. The structural uncertainties are represented by a probabilistic approach where all uncertain parameters are modeled by random variables with prescribed probability density functions. For structural systems with deterministic parameters, the multi-domain line sampling (mLS) method has emerged as a promising approach to estimate the failure probability. In order to evaluate the failure probability of uncertain structures, an integration over the probability space of the structural parameters is required. We propose an improved variant of the cross entropy-based importance sampling (CE-IS) method for first-passage problems to perform this integration that employs mLS to estimate the conditional first-passage probability for specific outcomes of the random parameters. The proposed approach is an adaptive sequential sampling approach that leverages on non-parametric regression of the approximate mLS estimates of the failure probability to locate the IS density over the important regions of the outcome space of the random parameters. Through numerical studies we demonstrate that the resulting method is robust and efficient when the failure event has several component failure modes or when the structural system has many degrees-of-freedom, e.g., finite element-based large-scale structural models.

title: Resilience evaluation of communication infrastructure networks under multi-scenario disaster simulations
Particle filter-based prognosis of damage propagation in laminates leveraging guided wave feature compression and interaction
A hybrid static–dynamic human reliability framework based on proportional hazard modeling and causally weighted performance shaping factors
A dual-bounded gamma model for infrastructure performance deterioration and maintenance effectiveness under missing condition data
A low-altitude emergency event grade prediction model integrating attention mechanism and spatio-temporal graph neural network
abstract: Low-altitude safety serves as a critical safeguard for the development of low-altitude economic activities, yet traditional early warning methods struggle to effectively address the complex spatiotemporal dynamic correlations during emergencies. This paper proposes a Low-altitude Emergency Level Prediction Model (GSTA-Net) that integrates attention mechanisms with spatiotemporal graph neural networks. By constructing an adaptive spatial domain graph that combines physical constraints with semantic associations, and designing a gated fusion mechanism incorporating dual spatial and temporal attention, the model achieves precise localization and efficient representation of dynamic spatiotemporal risk patterns. Experiments on an independently developed low-altitude safety dataset demonstrate that the model significantly outperforms mainstream spatiotemporal prediction models in key metrics such as macro-average F1 score and high-level event detection rate. The visualization of attention weights aligns closely with domain experts' analytical logic, showcasing excellent predictive accuracy and decision-making interpretability. This study provides an effective approach for building precise and reliable intelligent early warning systems for low-altitude operations.

title: Response of multi-dimensional dynamical system under combined Gaussian and Poisson white noise using tensor neural networks
abstract: Predicting the response density function of multi-dimensional systems under combined Gaussian and Poisson white noise excitations is of practical significance for characterizing the dynamic behavior of engineering systems. However, the forward Kolmogorov equation that governs the probability density function (PDF) of the system response is essentially an integro-differential equation (IDE) due to the jump characteristics of Poisson noise, posing significant challenges to the computational complexity and accuracy of traditional numerical methods in high-dimensional scenarios. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel Tensor Neural Networks-Physics-Informed Neural Networks (TNN-PINNs) learning framework, which integrates the low-rank decomposition properties of Tensor Neural Networks (TNNs) with the physics-constrained mechanisms of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to efficiently solve the reduced forward Kolmogorov equation of high-dimensional systems under Gaussian and Poisson white noises. The core of this framework lies in leveraging the low-rank decomposition properties of TNNs to achieve efficient and accurate computation of the integral terms, while utilizing the physics-constrained characteristics of PINNs to enhance the reliability and generalization ability of the solutions. The effectiveness of the framework is systematically validated in two-dimensional to six-dimensional spaces, addressing the challenge of balancing computational complexity and accuracy in traditional methods for high-dimensional problems.

title: Service reliability of intelligent computing cluster systems for large language models
abstract: Intelligent computing cluster system (ICCS) is a distributed computing infrastructure designed for training large language models (LLMs). Most of the existing reliability works on computing systems has predominantly focued on conventional architectures, such as generic data center networks and conventional cloud infrastructures. To our knowledge, the service reliability of new computing infrastructure, ICCS, has not been studied in literature. This paper bridges the gaps between academic research and industrial practice by developing a comprehensive service reliability framework for ICCS on LLM. The service reliability is defined from the perspective of the execution of parallelized training, taking into account the hybrid parallelism strategy of pipeline and data parallelism. The reliability assessment approach is developed concerning the inherent uncertainies on GPU performance. Meanwhile, to improve the service reliability metric, a reliability optimization problem is constructed to derive an optimal parallelism strategy, called RDpipe. The computational experiments are conducted to analyze the service reliability facing the different environmental settings. The results show that the derived RDpipe strategy has higher reliability and more stable performance than other classical parallelism strategies.

title: Active Kriging-based uniform importance sampling with rejection control for highly efficient and accurate structural reliability analysis
abstract: Developing highly efficient and accurate structural reliability analysis for high computational cost and low failure probability problems is critical for engineering application. In this paper, a novel active learning strategy coupling with weight control and adaptive distance control is proposed for Kriging-based uniform importance sampling. The rejection control is introduced to improve the efficiency of reliability analysis. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through numerical cases and three aerospace engineering applications, which showed that the proposed strategy could reduce both the cost of performance function evaluations and surrogate model calls. The repeated results validated that the proposed method is efficient, accurate, and robust, proving its capability to address real-world engineering challenges.

title: A failure-taxonomy-guided system-theoretic quantitative risk assessment framework for autonomous ship convoy navigation in inland waterways
Reliability and efficiency optimization of multi-product disassembly lines with destructive operations and preventive maintenance
A review on prognostics and health management applications with federated learning for advanced engineering systems
abstract: Modern engineering systems are increasingly complex and interconnected, making their health management and operational reliability more challenging. Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) enables condition monitoring, fault diagnosis, and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, yet conventional centralized approaches face regulatory barriers, privacy risks, and difficulty in modelling heterogeneous sensor data, while incurring high communication costs at the edge. Federated Learning (FL) offers a decentralized and privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative model training without raw data sharing. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of PHM technologies, FL methodologies, and their integration for distributed, privacy-sensitive industrial environments. We first survey advances in physics-based, data-driven, and hybrid prognostic methods, together with intelligent maintenance and condition-based decision strategies, critically evaluating their adaptability under heterogeneous, resource-constrained settings. We then classify FL approaches by data distribution, network architecture, and participant type, and assess their applicability to PHM tasks through quantitative comparison of privacy-preserving techniques and lightweight deployment strategies. Building on this, we establish a structured mapping between PHM challenges and FL mechanisms, analyse applications in RUL prediction, fault diagnosis, and health monitoring, and identify unresolved gaps. The review concludes with a forward-looking roadmap covering domain-adaptive FL algorithms, resource-efficient edge architectures, and verifiable privacy mechanisms, as well as integration with emerging technologies such as large language models and digital twins. By bridging methodological advances with industrial deployment realities, this work offers actionable guidance for developing scalable, secure, and high-performance PHM solutions in the Industrial Internet of Things era.

title: Hybrid maintenance optimization for multi-state competing failure systems under inspection uncertainties and spare dynamics
Dynamic response and resilience of unmanned aerial vehicle swarms under electromagnetic interference
A multi-damage coupling performance degradation reliability analysis method considering multi-source uncertainty
Integration of dynamic time-varying weighting and interpretable optimization modeling for practical degradation stage assessment
Spatial variability analysis of corroded pipelines using random fields: Degradation and reliability assessment
abstract: • A Gaussian Random Field was used to model pipeline corrosion and its variability • Spatial and temporal assessment of corrosion was proposed based on ILI data • Reliability was analyzed from a leak to support further pipe intervention decisions • The assessment incorporates uncertainty from ILI consecutive measurements • Critical segments can be spatially identified using the mean time to failure Corrosion in pipelines is inherently uncertain. Given the extensive infrastructures, not only a temporal but also a spatial assessment is required. Estimating and predicting the corrosion process in pipelines is essential for maintaining structural integrity and operational safety. Traditional methods typically focus on temporal assessments to predict corrosion degradation, and few studies examine how corrosion defects may interact spatially. This study presents a probabilistic degradation model using a Gaussian Random Field (GRF) to account for spatial and temporal variability of corrosion, using depth increments obtained from a matching approach. The GRF is simulated using the Cholesky decomposition for the covariance matrix, based on Gaussian and Exponential semivariogram fittings. These simulations were used jointly with a complementary Gamma Process to evaluate a leak limit state based on the defect depth. The proposed approach was applied to a 6 km section of a pipeline, which allows identifying the Mean Time to Failure when an isotropic (37 to 47 years), and an anisotropic (31 to 41 years) behavior is selected. This work seeks to support further decision-making regarding maintenance and monitoring processes to prevent any failure and consequences from a loss of containment.

title: Research on methane concentration prediction method based on non-steady-state feature coupling interaction and structural perception loss
Feature-prediction dual-space domain generalization framework for reliable RUL prediction of machinery
Beyond chronological time: Empirical validation of infusion-time reliability and latent risk detection in clinical infusion devices
Bionic job scheduling and resource management for cloud system considering co-resident attacks
Differentiated reinforcement strategies to improve seismic performance of electrical substations based on iterative sensitivity analysis
Risk-aware unsupervised cyberattack detection via contrastive autoencoding and adversarial training in smart grid substations
Risk predictive deduction and propagation chain mining for URT emergencies based on interpretable ensemble learning: A new approach to in-time safety management
abstract: To enhance the emergency response capability of Urban Rail Transit (URT), this paper proposes an in-time safety management approach based on explanatory ensemble learning and key risk chain mining. Firstly, an innovative in-time safety management framework is designed. On this basis, historical incident data from Beijing Metro in recent years is used to identify risk causation and impact range. A dynamic risk assessment and predictive deduction method based on explanatory Stacking ensemble learning model is designed. It incorporates Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) for sample balanced and Optuna for optimal hyperparameter tuning of both base and meta models, achieving superior prediction accuracy for risk impact levels. Then, SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) is employed to identify key risk causes and quantify their influence on prediction results. Finally, an improved W-Apriori algorithm is employed to mine the complex associations within key risk propagation chains, thereby providing targeted emergency response strategies. To demonstrate the approach, this paper presents a simulation case based on real operational emergency data and indicate that the proposed model achieves 95.83% accuracy, outperforming traditional machine learning methods across five performance metrics and exhibit superiority to promote a shift in URT safety management from traditional reactive response to proactive prevention and in-time intervention.

title: Causal-enhanced machine learning framework for long-term wind power probabilistic forecasting
abstract: Various and uncertain meteorological factors are the primary reason that makes long-term wind power forecasting formidable, which significantly constraints the reliability and economic viability of wind power. Evaluating the causal relationships between meteorological factors and wind power generation is a promising approach to addressing this issue. Therefore, we propose a novel day-ahead wind power forecasting framework that fuses a directed acyclic graph (DAG)–graph neural network (GNN) causal analysis model a data-driven long-term autoregressive model (autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA)–long short-term memory (LSTM)) and weather condition recognition model based on Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) algorithm to identify main meteorological features with influential causal effect on wind power then quantify uncertainty and perform time series wind power forecasting. An incremental learning strategy is employed to update and calibrate the prediction model continuously. The proposed framework is validated against real-world meteorological and wind power generation data from a wind farm in China. The experimental results demonstrate that this framework effectively captures the inherent uncertainty in long-term wind power forecasting, achieves high probabilistic forecasting performance, and exhibits high prediction accuracy.

title: Performance assessment of subway station structure considering site shear-wave velocity uncertainty using probability density evolution method
Multi-action predictive maintenance for lithium-ion batteries based on stacked bilinear neural network
abstract: Accurately predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of batteries and formulating predictive maintenance (PdM) decisions are essential for ensuring their reliable and efficient operation. However, most existing PdM studies rarely consider a unified framework that integrates probabilistic RUL prediction with short-term maintenance decision-making, making it difficult to meet the growing demands of modern industrial systems for intelligent maintenance. To address this gap, we propose a short-term multi-action PdM strategy driven by probabilistic RUL prediction. First, a stacked bilinear neural network (SBNN) is developed to extract both feature interactions and temporal degradation patterns from the measurement data. Then, by integrating quantile regression (QR) with kernel density estimation (KDE), a fully data-driven probabilistic representation of RUL is obtained. Based on the predicted RUL distribution, multi-action maintenance models are formulated for both single and multi-component systems, considering downtime, spare-part inventory and operating cycle length. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated using two real lithium-ion battery degradation datasets from MIT and Oxford. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RUL prediction method achieves the best performance in both point estimation and uncertainty quantification. Specifically, it attains an average RMSE of 13.7672 and an average PICP of 0.9552, outperforming several state-of-the-art baseline algorithms. Moreover, the proposed predictive maintenance strategy can effectively prevent component-level failures and reduce system-level maintenance costs.

title: Multi-sensor spatial and multiscale temporal transformer guided by frequency-domain attention for aeroengine remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for aeroengine prognostics and health management. However, standard Transformer-based models struggle to capture multiscale temporal dynamics and cross-sensor dependencies in aeroengine sensors. Moreover, time-domain scaled dot-product attention does not exploit the degradation characteristics of onboard sensor series or the low-rank structure evident in the frequency domain. We propose Multi-sensor Spatial and Multiscale Temporal Transformer guided by Frequency-Domain Attention (MSMT-FDA), which couples a dual-branch encoder-encompassing multiscale temporal cues and multi-sensor spatial correlations-with frequency-domain low-rank distance attention, leveraging spectral low-rank priors of engine degradation signals. On C-MAPSS (FD001-FD004) and DS02 of N-CMAPSS, our method attains state-of-the-art performance and remains robust across flight regimes, enabling predictive maintenance.

title: Mutual information-guided causal feature selection method for quality prediction of complex products
Resilience performance analysis of interdependent infrastructures using Fault Tree and Dynamic Bayesian Network
abstract: Interdependent infrastructure systems are designed to work synergistically, but disruptions in one can rapidly propagate to others, posing significant challenges to their stable operation. This study introduces a novel integrated probabilistic modelling framework for simulating the resilience performance of interdependent infrastructures. The proposed computational model employs a Fault Tree to interpret complex relationships among interdependent infrastructures, identify cascading failure propagation paths, and calculate component failure probabilities in non-disaster scenarios. Building on the static cascading failure analysis provided by the fault tree, a hybrid Dynamic Bayesian Networks model is developed to assess the dynamic resilience of interdependent infrastructures, incorporating both constant nodes (unaffected by disasters) and time-dependent nodes (affected by disasters). The proposed computational model is applied to a real community-scale water–electricity–road (WER) system in China, with a focus on physical interdependences. Under non-disaster conditions, the probability of water-supply failure (1.89%) exceeds that of electricity supply (0.67%) and road accessibility (0.58%), with ageing sub-pipelines identified as critical vulnerable components. Under rainfall scenarios, resilience performance loss increases nonlinearly with rainfall intensity, with the road system exhibiting the most rapid degradation, followed by the electricity and water systems. These results support a sequenced recovery and mitigation strategy that prioritises roads, followed by electricity, and then water. Overall, this study provides a novel integrated probabilistic model to identify critical physical interdependencies, assess time-iterative resilience performance, and compare recovery strategies, thereby supporting resilience-informed decision-making for disaster mitigation and protection of critical infrastructures.

title: Research on emergency supplies scheduling using an enhanced demand forecasting model and alternative subgraph theory
An efficient multi-output global sensitivity analysis based on vector-form homotopy surrogate model
abstract: For complex engineering structures, the optimal design and construction control usually require consideration of various responses at different parts of the structure. Therefore, the global sensitivity analysis (GSA) conducted for multiple outputs is of great significance. However, the costly model evaluations and response diversity pose challenges to the efficiency and accuracy of GSA. This study proposes a sample-free, vector-form surrogate modeling framework for efficient multi-output GSA of linear static structural systems. Specifically, through the homotopy stochastic finite element method, the multiple responses of the structure subjected to the static load are represented as linear combinations of deterministic vector coefficients and basis functions of the random variables. To quantify the random input effect on the multi-output, the covariance decomposition-based sensitivity index adopted from the literature is written in an equivalent variance-weighted aggregation of componentwise Sobol’ indices, which is computed efficiently through closed-form matrix operations involving the surrogate coefficients and moment-based covariance information of the basis functions. Numerical examples, including GSA of the multiple static responses of a reinforced concrete-steel column and a large-span cable-stayed bridge, illustrate the proposed method's excellent calculation efficiency and numerical stability by comparing to the Kriging, polynomial chaos expansion, and their principal component analysis-based variants.

title: State variance-based uncertainty quantification in structural response via Malliavin formulation
Robust probabilistic estimating remaining useful life by considering aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty on health index data
Real-time inversion of radioactive source distribution using air dose rate measurements via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator method
A Chen-distribution-based Wiener process for nonlinear degradation processes with likelihood-free Bayesian inference

Corrigendum to “Deep foundation pit excavation risk identification and mitigation using knowledge graph integrated with domain knowledge and monitoring data” [Reliability Engineering & System Safety, Volume 274 (2026) 112415]
A new sequential optimization and reliability assessment framework with dynamic penalty coefficients for reliability-based co-design optimization problems
A collision risk-based method for safety distance recommendation for offshore platforms and navigation routes considering ships out-of-control
Enhancing data integrity for autonomous ships: A multi-level detection model against clean-label poisoning attacks
Efficient rare event estimation for multimodal and high-dimensional system reliability via subset adaptive importance sampling
abstract: Estimating rare events in complex systems is a key challenge in reliability analysis. The challenge grows in multimodal problems, where traditional methods often rely on a small set of design points and risk overlooking critical failure modes. Further, higher dimensions make the probability mass harder to capture and demand substantially larger sample sizes to estimate failures. In this work, we propose a new sampling strategy, subset adaptive importance sampling (SAIS), that combines the strengths of subset simulation and adaptive multiple importance sampling. SAIS iteratively refines a set of proposal distributions using weighted samples from previous stages, efficiently exploring complex and high-dimensional failure regions. Leveraging recent advances in adaptive importance sampling, SAIS yields low-variance estimates using fewer samples than state-of-the-art methods and achieves pronounced improvements in both accuracy and computational cost. Through a series of benchmark problems involving high-dimensional, nonlinear performance functions, and multimodal scenarios, we demonstrate that SAIS consistently outperforms competing methods in capturing diverse failure modes and estimating failure probabilities with high precision.

title: Predictive maintenance scheduling of recoverable stochastic hybrid systems under degradation and shocks: A case study of an offshore wind farm
abstract: • Extend the SHS model with recoverability and derive analytical solutions. • Derive a Markov control policy to maximize long-term asset value. • Infer failure mechanisms to support PdM under stochastic conditions. • Validate the PdM plan on a simulated 16-turbine offshore wind farm. Predictive maintenance (PdM) is recognized as a next-generation maintenance paradigm across industrial applications. However, implementing PdM in complex engineering systems, such as an offshore wind farm, remains highly challenging. These systems are exposed to continuous degradation and external shocks simultaneously and also feature recoverability. Meanwhile, they often exhibit failure interactions, such as common cause failures (CCFs) and dependent or competing failures. These characteristics hinder accurate condition assessment and complicate maintenance planning. To address these challenges, this study extends the stochastic hybrid system (SHS) framework to model the reliability of repairable systems with self-recovery capability under degradation and shock-induced CCFs. Furthermore, a PdM scheduling approach is proposed based on a Markov control policy that maximizes the expected asset value and determines optimal health levels under stochastic market conditions. A case study is conducted on a simulated offshore wind farm with 16 turbines exposed to lethal and non-lethal shocks. Partially observed data from simulations are used to estimate a transition matrix and predict system states for PdM decisions. The objective function minimizes the discrepancy between the estimated Markov control policy and turbine conditions through maintenance actions. The results show that the predicted optimal maintenance plan closely matches the theoretical optimal plan.

title: Human-vehicle collaborative evacuation strategies in coal mine fire emergencies: A social force model approach
Convolutional attention channel factorization mixing network-based state of health estimation for lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Accurately estimating the state of health (SOH) is critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, the performance of existing methods is often compromised by redundant information present in monitoring data. To address this issue, we propose a novel method for SOH estimation based on a convolutional attention channel factorization mixing network (CACFMN). This method consists of a feature extraction module, several channel factorization mixture and temporal processing (CFMTP) modules, and an estimator module. Specifically, a dual-branch convolutional attention module is established to adaptively capture health characteristics from the charging data of LIBs. Furthermore, the CFMTP module is designed to reduce redundancy among the various channels of these characteristics. Subsequently, the estimator module is developed to estimate the SOH of LIBs. Finally, the proposed method was validated using three battery datasets that employed distinct materials and charging-discharging strategies. The experimental results indicate that the designed CFMTP module effectively reduces redundant information across channels, thereby enhancing the accuracy and generalizability of SOH estimation.

title: Dynamic framework for crew dispatch optimization in power distribution fault inspection
abstract: • Fault location: This paper presents a framework for locating faults using inspection crews. • Bayes’ Theorem: Trouble calls are used to estimate the posterior probability of faults. • Multi-objective model: A multi-objective model is proposed for dispatching inspection crews. • Dynamic framework: A dynamic method updates the posterior fault probabilities using field information provided by crews and updates routes accordingly. • Efficiency: The use of posterior probability can reduce inspection time. The increasing frequency of natural disasters in recent years has significantly affected electrical distribution networks. A growing body of research has focused on dispatching crews to inspect and repair the electrical grid. While some studies estimate fault probabilities, others incorporate trouble calls or propose dynamic, multi-objective approaches. However, existing studies do not integrate all these aspects into a unified framework that simultaneously refines fault probabilities based on trouble calls, updates them dynamically using field inspection information, and embeds the updated probabilities into a multi-objective optimization model. Most existing approaches address these elements separately, for example by estimating prior fault probabilities without dynamic updating or by optimizing crew routing primarily based on shortest paths. As a result, such approaches may delay the inspection of the most likely fault locations and limit the effectiveness of inspection. This gap is addressed in this work and validated through numerical experiments. This paper proposes a dynamic bi-objective model for dispatching crews to inspect outaged areas, aiming to minimize routing efforts while prioritizing areas with higher fault probabilities. The problem is addressed using a lexicographic method, which first optimizes one objective and then solves the second without altering the result of the first. To support the model, posterior fault probabilities are estimated using Bayes’ theorem and updated with trouble call and field information, allowing adaptive crew routing. Numerical experiments on the IEEE-34 and IEEE-126 test systems demonstrate that dynamic refinement of fault probabilities, driven by inspection crew feedback, leads to substantial improvements in fault detection time.

title: Reliability assessment for a Vehicle-to-Grid mode system with performance sharing
Incorporating analogy and adaptation into cognitive model for risk assessment in emergency scenarios without pre-established operating procedures
Dynamic risk analysis of bunkering operations based on system dynamics simulation and Bayesian network
abstract: • A dynamic risk assessment method involving system dynamics simulation and Bayesian network is proposed • The system dynamics model enables dynamic probability prediction under the coupling mechanism of faults • A Bayesian network-based consequence model is established to assess the effect of safety barriers • A case study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed methodology for methanol bunkering under SIMOPs • The societal risks associated with methanol leakage are assessed across varying population densities This paper proposes a dynamic risk assessment method based on system dynamics (SD) simulation to deal with both the complexity of systems involving simultaneous operations (SIMOPs) and their dynamic evolution over time. A fault tree model is constructed and transformed into an SD model comprising four feedback loops, enabling dynamic probability prediction under coupling mechanisms while accounting for each loss of containment (LOC). Critical hazard factors are identified and ranked based on mutual information (MI), allowing prioritization of safety interventions. Consequence-probability modelling is carried out by establishing a Bayesian network (BN)-based event tree considering safety barriers (SBs). The severity of potential consequences is evaluated using fire modelling in ALOHA. Individual and societal risk values are subsequently calculated, followed by the development of risk mitigation measures at a bunkering station in the Port of Shanghai, China, as a practical case study. The proposed mitigation strategies effectively reduce leakage probability and associated risks. The proposed framework effectively characterizes the temporal evolution of risk, provides enhanced representation of time-dependent risk dynamics compared with traditional static quantitative risk assessment models, and offers a transferable basis for alternative marine fuels and port operations. To the best of our knowledge, the combination of bow-tie analysis, dynamic simulation, and Bayesian networks for temporal methanol bunkering risk assessment remains unexplored in the current academic literature.

title: Team-dynamics-informed machine learning: Exploring team dynamic patterns of critical team actions in unstable approach cases using role-specific shared mental models
abstract: Unstable approaches during landing are critical aviation events often associated with ineffective coordination between pilots and air traffic controllers (ATCOs). Shared mental models (SMMs) of common goals are essential for effective teamwork. However, SMM inconsistency alone does not explain coordination breakdowns in heterogeneous teams. The current study introduces role-specific SMM as an interaction-dependent construct that captures teamwork compatibility by characterizing the alignment of individual knowledge with coordination demands imposed by rolespecific goal orientations. It developed a team-dynamics-informed machine learning (TDIML) framework based on this construct. This framework integrates survey-based cognitive data with machine learning techniques to uncover patterns across scenario contexts, individual mental models, SMMs, and role-specific SMMs. Contextual modeling was conducted using a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) structured into three layers: scenario, team dynamics, and team operations. Survey data were collected from 30 pilots and 11 ATCOs. Unsupervised learning revealed two dominant team dynamic patterns: early-phase ATCO-driven air traffic management and latephase reactive synchronization. Supervised learning and explainable artificial intelligence revealed the cognitive mechanisms underlying these patterns. Moreover, DBN analysis demonstrated that role-specific SMMs link scenario changes to operational decisions. Overall, the findings underscore the importance of role-specific SMMs in heterogeneous socio-technical systems, demonstrating that these models capture deficiencies in team dynamics that cannot be explained by SMM inconsistency alone. Furthermore, the TDIML framework can serve as a basis for designing training modules that enhance role-specific SMM compatibility.

title: A novel time-varying Wiener process for adaptive RUL prediction under multiple uncertainties
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for high-reliability complex systems is often challenged by scarce real degradation data and noise-contaminated simulated data, limiting the ability of existing methods to handle multiple uncertainties and time-varying characteristics, which in turn constrains the robustness and interpretability of predictions. This study proposes a time-varying Wiener process (TVWP) degradation model that incorporates the quantification of multiple uncertainties. First, a TVWP model is developed to characterize dynamic degradation patterns, taking into full account unit-to-unit variability and time-varying degradation behaviors. Second, a normal cloud model-based Bayesian parameter estimation method is designed to achieve adaptive updating of time-varying parameters and dynamic quantification of epistemic uncertainty. Finally, the probability distribution of the RUL is derived analytically, enabling adaptive prediction while simultaneously achieving real-time quantification of prediction errors and uncertainty. The proposed method is validated on a small-sample gyroscope drift dataset and the large-scale C-MAPSS benchmark. Results demonstrate its strong adaptability to different data volumes and significant superiority over conventional Wiener process models and state-of-the-art approaches in both prediction accuracy and robustness.

title: Joint condition-based maintenance and production of manufacturing systems under flexible decision timing using deep reinforcement learning
abstract: In manufacturing systems, deterioration increases the risk of unmet demand due to reduced product quality and increased downtime. To sustain high productivity and effectively meet demand, efficient coordination between maintenance and production decisions is essential. However, conventional policies typically do not adjust production decisions in response to system deterioration, which can lead to decreased productivity and service levels. This paper proposes a novel and well-motivated framework for the joint decision-making of maintenance and production in parallel manufacturing systems, formulated as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP). Specifically, we incorporate flexible decision timing that allows real-time adjustments to production speeds whenever system deterioration occurs, in order to maintain a high demand fulfillment rate. To solve the resulting large-scale decision-making problem, characterized by a high-dimensional information space encompassing system condition, inventory, demand, and maintenance status, we apply a deep reinforcement learning algorithm: heterogeneous-agent proximal policy optimization (HAPPO). Numerical discussion shows that the proposed method, which derives the joint policy with flexible decision timing and production speed control using HAPPO, outperforms three alternative methods. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that flexible production speed control not only increases total rewards but also improves demand fulfillment. The proposed joint decision-making framework offers a practical and effective solution for deteriorating systems, contributing to the development of more resilient and adaptive manufacturing operations.

title: Spatiotemporal causal modeling of cascading failures in power systems
abstract: • A spatiotemporal causal model is proposed for cascading failure analysis. • A novel counterfactual method performs robust root cause analysis of cascades. • Causal metrics guide more efficient grid hardening than traditional methods. • Causal metrics identify critical components for robust system monitoring. The interconnected nature of modern power grids makes them susceptible to cascading failures, complex events that can trigger widespread blackouts. Data-driven analysis of these events is often limited by an undue on statistical correlation, which hinders model explainability and prevents true root cause analysis. This paper proposes a spatiotemporal causal inference framework that learns the underlying cause-and-effect mechanisms of failure propagation from historical data. The proposed Structural Causal Model enables forward-looking prediction, backward-looking root cause analysis via counterfactuals, and guides grid reinforcement through causal metrics. Results on standard literature test cases validate the framework’s effectiveness. The model achieves high prediction accuracy (84.29%), outperforming several benchmarks, and correctly identifies the initial failure in over 70% of scenarios. Furthermore, a hardening strategy guided by causal metrics is shown to be significantly more efficient than traditional approaches, requiring less than half the number of reinforced components to achieve a comparable level of system reliability. The proposed framework offers a robust, explainable, and actionable methodology for understanding and mitigating cascading failures.

title: Physics-informed multi-task generation: Toward automated risk control optimization
abstract: Automated risk control measure generation is crucial for safety and reliability in complex engineering systems. Traditional expert-based methods are labor-intensive and subjective. While large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong general capabilities, their specialized-domain outputs lack reliability due to limited domain knowledge. To address these challenges, we propose a physics-informed multi-task generation (PIMTG) framework that integrates physical constraints of risk propagation with deep learning. PIMTG enables co-optimized generation of three risk control measures: engineering interventions, safety management strategies, and emergency preparedness protocols, enhancing both textual quality and physical rationality. Specifically, we first develop a gated fusion mechanism with adaptive attention for heterogeneous features (textual, numerical, categorical). Additionally, we propose a multi-task prefix adapter to generate different risk control measures. Finally, we develop a training objective incorporating risk energy and evolution constraint equations, jointly minimizing text generation loss and physical consistency loss. This ensures that risk source terms, diffusion terms, absorption terms, and inherent risk values comply with first principles. On real industrial cases, PIMTG achieves an average BERTScore of 78.75%, a physical consistency index of 99.9%, and a symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) of 0.0448, demonstrating its accuracy and reliability in automated risk control.

title: Analysing power system cascading failures and service disruptions in a data-scarce environment: A case study of Vietnam
abstract: Cascading failures in power grids can escalate localized disruptions into extensive service outages. This study presents a transparent, reproducible framework to build power grids from publicly available data, integrating commissioned power plants, substations, transmission lines, and hypothetical transformers, for large-scale power system modelling. To assess how grid disruptions lead to service interruptions for industrial users, we combine Google Places API industrial points of interest with OpenStreetMap industrial zones, and link them to substations based on capacity and proximity. We model initial disruptions under two scenarios: 1) random disruptions, implemented through percolation analysis to assess network robustness under stochastic component removals; and 2) targeted disruptions, generated by Monte Carlo sampling of wind-induced fragility curves derived from the 2024 Typhoon Yagi wind field to produce probabilistic failures. The analysis reveals distinct spatial variation in grid vulnerability and traces the propagation of failures through the network, quantifying downstream service disruptions for industrial users. System-wide simulations further identify critical transmission corridors with higher failure and overload risks. These insights provide a basis for targeted investment, resilience assessment, and future research on multi-hazard and adaptive protection strategies.

title: A two-dimensional traffic conflict measurement for assessing the safety of light mobility vehicles
abstract: • This study proposed a 2D-TTC approach to better suit LMVs’ safety applications • A case study was conducted in an urban midblock • 2D-TTC had a better traffic conflicts and crashes relationship compared to TTC • Bicycles were more often involved in potential rear-end and sideswipe conflicts • Two-dimensional kinematic data are important for assessing traffic conflict Light Mobility Vehicles (LMVs) are vulnerable road users due to limited protection and low stability. Understanding their rear-end and sideswipe crash risks is crucial for designing effective safety interventions. To assess the crash risks, a two-dimensional Time to Collision (2D-TTC) approach has been developed. Nevertheless, the existing equation was impractical in LMV-related situations. This study aims to develop a 2D-TTC approach to more effectively suit LMVs’ safety applications. A case study was conducted at an urban mid-block location in Melbourne, Australia. Extreme Value Theory was employed to model the relationship between traffic conflicts and crashes. 2D-TTC and Time to Collision (TTC) thresholds were also identified. The case study results showed that 2D-TTC approach had a closer traffic conflict-crash relationship compared to the traditional TTC function. The findings also indicated that bicycles were more frequently involved in rear-end and sideswipe conflicts compared to motorcycles and e-bikes. This study demonstrated the importance of considering two-dimensional kinematic data for assessing traffic conflicts of LMVs. Future practical applications with a larger dataset may provide insights for the use of 2D-TTC for assessing traffic safety, reinforcing LMV users’ awareness of minimum safety gaps when following a leading vehicle and promoting LMV’ warning systems.

title: Efficient probabilistic 3D slope stability assessment considering the depth-adjusted non-stationary soil parameters
Road network resilience assessment based on full-scenario disaster simulation: landslide movement, emergency, and stabilization
Artificial intelligence-driven framework for predicting cascading failure paths in power grids
abstract: As evidenced by large-scale blackouts with severe economic impacts, cascading failures remain a critical challenge that demands intelligent methods to detect hidden propagation paths before they escalate. This work proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework that encompasses codified data generation, methodical model comparison, meticulous hyperparameter optimization, and holistic performance evaluation for propagation paths prediction. Using training data generated under diverse operating conditions for power systems, including IEEE 39, 89, 118 and 300-bus models, this study investigates the performance of decision tree, logistic regression (LogR), k-nearest neighbor, support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) in predicting cascading failure paths, alongside a comparative analysis with the influence model and graph neural networks using graph-level and branch-level accuracy metrics and efficiency metrics, as well as a proposed composite reliability index. To further improve model performance, Bayesian optimization is applied for hyperparameters tuning of the AI methods. Comprehensive numerical experiments are performed, revealing that MLP, SVM, and LogR consistently achieve robust performance while the other models exhibit vulnerabilities under moderate load scaling conditions. The proposed framework can support industry stakeholders in selecting and deploying suitable AI methods for cascading failure prediction in real-world power grid applications.

title: Multi-player stag hunt game in hypergraph
Towards intelligent safety assessment under blast loading: A large language model-powered multi-agent framework
abstract: Reliable and timely safety assessment under blast loading constitutes a critical, expertise-driven challenge, requiring the accurate evaluation of damage effects on specific targets under prescribed conditions. Despite advances in related fields, such as ammunition theory and vulnerability analysis, fully reliable and intelligent safety assessment systems are still in their fancy. This study proposes a novel framework that integrates large language model (LLM) reasoning with multi-agent coordination, featuring domain expertise embedded in customized safety assessment tools, which eliminates the dependency on large-scale training datasets. Experiments across diverse LLM scales, query complexities, and target conditions demonstrate the excellent stability and adaptability of the proposed framework to autonomously complete complex tasks without human intervention. An empirical investigation of system-level target safety assessment substantiates the necessity of an agentic design framework, as the standalone LLM fails to produce correct results even despite employing detailed chain-of-thought reasoning. Complementary evidence from a case study on component-level targets further underscores the importance of the multi-agent architecture. Specifically, the simplified dual-agent configuration struggles to effectively handle more complex task demands. This study highlights the potential of combining artificial intelligence with traditional methodologies, offering a promising pathway for advancing safety assessment and its engineering applications.

title: Probabilistic assessment of multi-mode failure of levees under climate change
Human-Hardware-in-the-Loop simulations for systemic resilience assessment in cyber-socio-technical systems
abstract: Modern industrial systems require updated safety management approaches, as the tight interplay between cyber-physical, human, and organizational factors has driven their processes toward increasing complexity. In addition to dealing with known risks, managing system resilience acquires great value to address complex behaviours pragmatically. This manuscript starts from the System-Theoretic Accident Model and Processes (STAMP) as a modelling initiative for such complexity. The STAMP can be natively integrated with simulation-based approaches, which however fail to realistically represent human behaviours and their influence on the system performance. To overcome this limitation, this research proposes a Human-Hardware-in-the-Loop (HHIL) modelling and simulation framework aimed at supporting a more realistic and comprehensive assessment of systemic resilience. The approach is tested on an experimental oil and gas plant experiencing cyber-attacks, where two personas of operators (experts and novices) work. The obtained results provide a means to quantitatively assess how variations in operators’ behaviours impact the overall system performance, offering insights into how resilience should be understood and implemented in complex socio-technical systems at large.

title: Resilience analysis of urban cyber-physical-social systems: Insights from the 2023 Beijing rainstorm
Predicting seismic floor response for nuclear power plant structures with time-series uncertainty propagation using attention-enhanced multimodal deep learning
abstract: • Fuse ground motion and structural parameters using cross-modal attention. • Enable real-time probabilistic analysis by replacing expensive FEA with a surrogate model. • Predict full probabilistic time-histories at multiple structural locations. • Transform risk assessment from binary classification to continuous quantification. • Achieve high fidelity ( R 2 > 0.98) with a mean prediction error below 1.4%. Ensuring the safety and reliability of critical equipment in nuclear power plants (NPPs) requires accounting for uncertainties in structural parameters. However, probabilistic methods based on finite element analysis (FEA) can be computationally expensive and impractical for real-time safety assessment. In this study, we propose a surrogate framework based on deep learning that directly generates full time-history acceleration responses at multiple structural locations to reduce the computational cost of probabilistic analysis by replacing FEA. The architecture is organized into two encoders, including a structural parameter encoder and a seismic encoder enabling feature extraction from two distinct input modalities. Their latent representations are fused and mapped using a response decoder that reconstructs multi-output acceleration responses. The results of experimental validation show that the model achieved an average maximum mean absolute percentage error (mMAPE) of 1.37%. Beyond deterministic surrogate predictions, the proposed framework generates probabilistic responses to capture the variability of structural response over time and instantly estimate exceedance probabilities with respect to equipment-level thresholds. This probabilistic inspection capability extends conventional deterministic safety checks to a reliability-informed paradigm to offer a computationally efficient solution for the assessment of important equipment in NPPs.

title: The impact of natural hazards on the security of chemical sites
abstract: • The performance of security elements impacted by natural hazards is investigated. • Quantitative data were obtained through expert elicitation. • Failure probabilities exceed 70% in the case of earthquakes and floods. • Routing time more than doubles in the presence of natural hazards. • Downtime due to natural hazards may increase vulnerability to physical attacks. The protection of chemical sites from intentional malicious attacks, as theft, arson, and sabotage, is of utmost importance, due to the high potential hazards deriving from the mismanagement of the hazardous substances handled and stored. Highly effective Physical Protection Systems (PPS) are usually installed to ensure the security of chemical sites. Specific approaches as Security Vulnerability Assessment (SVA) and Security Risk Assessment (SRA) are applied to manage security issues. However, while the impact of natural hazards on the safety of chemical sites has been extensively studied, their influence on security elements remains largely unexplored. In the present study, the potential impact of 7 different natural hazards on 17 physical barriers, technological systems, and procedures constituting the PPS of chemical sites is addressed. Expert elicitation has been used to quantitatively assess the possibility and probability of failure of security elements due to the impact of natural hazards. A survey was carried out, involving 61 respondents with multidisciplinary background and expertise. The likelihood of damage of the security elements considered estimated in the survey is on average 10% and is higher than 40% for specific components. Performance modification factors, expressing the probability of damage or impairment of a security element following the impact of a specific natural hazard, resulted comprised between 0.25 and 0.95, evidencing the potential severe impact of natural hazards on PPS. Overall, the results obtained contribute to the assessment and management of security risks in chemical sites, underscoring the need for holistic and synergic strategies to enhance security and safety towards the impact of natural hazards.

title: Spatiotemporal seismic performance-informed evolution of corroded long-distance natural gas pipelines
Surface decomposition method for sensitivity analysis of first-passage dynamic reliability of linear systems
abstract: This work presents a novel surface decomposition method for the sensitivity analysis of first-passage dynamic reliability of linear systems subjected to Gaussian random excitations. The method decomposes the sensitivity of first-passage failure probability into a sum of surface integrals over the constrained component limit-state hypersurfaces. The evaluation of these surface integrals can be accomplished, owing to the availability of closed-form linear expressions of both the component limit-state functions and their sensitivities for linear systems. An importance sampling strategy is introduced to further enhance the efficiency for estimating the sum of these surface integrals. The number of function evaluations required for the reliability sensitivity analysis is typically on the order of 10^2 to 10^3. The approach is particularly advantageous when a large number of design parameters are considered, as the results of function evaluations can be reused across different parameters. Three numerical examples are investigated to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Optimal transmission system repair considering distribution system damage and evacuations
A hybrid human reliability level prediction model study on human-computer interaction in a main control room of NPPs
Adaptive and robust scheduling subject to machine degradation and breakdowns in networked multi-factory systems via hierarchical multi-head deep reinforcement learning
abstract: In equipment-intensive manufacturing, machine degradation and breakdowns threaten system robustness and production continuity, while multi-layer couplings and dynamic collaboration in mass-customized networked multi-factory systems exacerbate these challenges. This study addresses the robust scheduling problem for networked multi-factory systems with machine degradation and breakdowns under mass customization (MC-NMFRS-MDB) and proposes a hierarchical multi-head deep reinforcement learning (HMH-DRL) approach. The problem is formulated as a multi-Markov decision process with a high-dimensional state space capturing degradation and breakdown dynamics, a dual-layer action space addressing coupled subproblems, and a multi-head reward balancing performance and robustness. A hierarchical multi-head policy architecture enables coordinated decision-making and multi-objective optimization. The training process employs prioritized experience replay to improve learning efficiency, nonlinear clipping to stabilize policy updates, and a retraining mechanism for continual adaptation. Numerical results indicate that HMH-DRL reliably converges, improving scheduling performance and robustness by over 10.59% and 10.98%, respectively, compared with four DRL methods, three metaheuristic algorithms, and one reliability-driven heuristic, confirming its effectiveness in complex and dynamic scenarios.

title: An investigation of miners’ safety situational awareness across multiple contexts and human reliability assessment using an integrated Extreme Gradient Boosting and Borderline Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique
abstract: Understanding miners’ situational awareness and its impact on hazard identification is vital for enhancing human reliability in high-risk settings. Previous studies have primarily emphasized behavioural data, with limited incorporation of physiological indicators. This study adopted the Lawrence safety model and adapted it into a five-stage hazard-identification framework to examine miners’ cognitive–behavioural processes, with predictive validity evaluated using a machine-learning approach. A hazard-identification experiment involving 68 male miners was conducted, collecting behavioural measures (accuracy and reaction time) and eye-tracking metrics (fixation duration and fixation count) across decision-making stages. The results indicated that miners with higher SA exhibited longer reaction times but higher accuracy in hazard recognition and accident judgment. Their gaze patterns were more widely distributed and showed greater attention to key areas of interest. Furthermore, an XGBoost classifier combined with borderline-SMOTE achieved an accuracy of 84 % in distinguishing SA levels under small-sample conditions. Overall, the findings suggest that integrating behavioural and eye-tracking data provides an effective means of characterising individual differences in SA, and the proposed hybrid approach offers a proof of concept for SA assessment, providing methodological insights for future research on intelligent monitoring and early-warning approaches in mining contexts.

title: Human intelligence collaboration reliability: perception time distributions under under-trust for evaluation of human error of visual neglect
Evaluating minimal cut sets and the Fussell-Vesely measure of component importance using the Dynamic and Dependant Tree Theory methodology
abstract: Dynamic and Dependant Tree Theory (D 2 T 2 ) is a recent advance in fault tree analysis (FTA) which increases its ability to represent features commonly encountered on modern industrial systems. These advances are achieved by integrating the capabilities of Binary Decision Diagrams, Stochastic Petri Nets and Markov models so that the most appropriate modelling technique is used for each part of the assessment. Currently, the D 2 T 2 framework can predict the system failure probability and failure frequency, along with the Birnbaum, Criticality, Risk Achievement Worth and Risk Reduction Worth measures of component importance. In this paper, the focus is on extending the D 2 T 2 methodology to deliver the Fussell-Vesely (FV) measure of component importance. This measure of importance is defined in terms of the probability of the fault tree’s minimal cut sets. Whilst, for traditional FTA, the minimal cut sets are produced at an intermediate stage in the analysis, they are not calculated in the D 2 T 2 methodology. If they are required, additional processing must be performed. It will be demonstrated that the modularisation employed in D 2 T 2 , with each basic event appearing in only one mutually independent module, makes this a very efficient extension. The FV measures can be calculated directly from the minimal cut sets using a fast, accurate, approximation. For situations where summary information, giving the total number of minimal cut sets and the number of each order, is preferred to a full listing, a method, based on a polynomial formulation is presented.

title: Prediction of system level failure probabilities of printed circuit boards under vibration load using simulation-based failure mode and effects analysis
abstract: The effects of vibration loads on the reliability of printed circuit boards is gaining importance due to the increasing use in vibration-intensive areas such as the drive train of electric cars. When assessing the reliability of electronic systems, it is important to consider not only the general probability of failures, but also their effects at the system level. Different failure modes present varying degrees of safety risk, which is taken into account in the design process through target values for failure probabilities. However, the occurrence probabilities of specific failure modes are currently assessed mainly qualitatively, or based on literature values and expert estimations. This work presents a simulation-based failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA) to estimate the probability of failure modes depending on external vibration loads. The simulation-based FMEA combines a numerical simulation, a lifetime model and a probabilistic FMEA. The key to reliable estimations of failure probabilities is the quantification of uncertainties that cause variations of the structural dynamic properties and thereby variations of local stresses on the electronic components. Therefore, Bayesian model updating is conducted to find probability distributions representing the scattering of selected parameters. The method is applied to a test printed circuit board and validated with experimental failure data.

title: A deep-learning-based approach for temporal transportation network dismantling
abstract: Accurately assessing the importance of individual nodes at different time for maintaining the efficiency of temporal transportation networks is an important challenging problem. It is for the first time that this issue has been formulated as a temporal network dismantling (ND) problem, which aims to identify the minimal set of nodes with time information whose disruption can rapidly degrade temporal network efficiency. This paper proposes a deep-learning-based network dismantling framework for its solution. Specifically, a directed acyclic graph representation is used to capture the continuous topological changes in a temporal network. Then, our framework employs multi-head graph attention networks to learn latent higher-order features by aggregating different temporal features of nodes and their neighbors, and incorporates the shortcut connections technique to mitigate the vanishing gradient problem. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world networks demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms baselines and exhibits significant robustness. Furthermore, an early warning signal indicator is adopted to quantify the dismantling risk of temporal networks. Our approach offers a practical tool for identifying critical nodes in temporal transportation networks, thereby assisting stakeholders in enhancing robustness of transportation services.

title: Editorial Board
Hybrid simulation-optimization approach for power distribution systems resilience assessment
abstract: • Resilience assessment needs systemic approaches to account for DS’s features; • Service restoration does not necessarily enhance resilience; • Resilience uncertainty varies for each distribution system and enhancement strategy; • Robust resilience enhancement needs to consider the inherent uncertainty. Electrical power is central to our modern society, and minimal delivery disruption underlies other critical systems ranging from healthcare to defense. Consequently, power distribution systems’ resilience is a strategic field, with resilience assessment playing a vital role in understanding and planning resilience enhancement strategies for this complex system. This paper presents a simulation-optimization approach to assess power distribution systems’ resilience. The method combines a Monte Carlo simulation to obtain failure and repair times for weather conditions and a metaheuristic to derive a service restoration plan for each component’s state transition during resilience estimation. We demonstrate the approach’s applicability on two example distribution systems under mild, adverse, and extreme weather scenarios. We evaluate the effect of service restoration during resilience estimation alone and in the presence of distributed generation in a grid-connected mode for two distribution systems. In addition to showing emergent resilience due to service restoration and distributed generation integration, which differ for each system, a resampling experiment is conducted to investigate the uncertainty around usual resilience metrics. Results show the benefits of our method in comprehensively assessing power distribution systems’ resilience and highlight the need to carefully examine the uncertainty associated with resilience indices during assessment or enhancement studies.

title: Optimal patching policies for software systems considering dynamic user adoption
Optimizing community-led post-disaster recovery in flood-affected areas: A resilience model for volunteer deployment
abstract: Effective post-disaster recovery relies heavily on volunteers, yet coordinating their deployment over extended recovery horizons remains operationally challenging and costly. This paper presents a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for planning volunteer deployment during flood recovery, integrating mobilization, team formation, operational deployment, and outsourcing costs within a single optimization framework. The formulation schedules volunteer teams to disaster-affected regions across multiple days, prioritizes higher-urgency areas through severity-weighted service timing, and enforces practical operational constraints including daily team capacity limits, group activation logic, and precedence relations among regions, while retaining an explicit choice between internal deployment and external outsourcing under limited volunteer capacity. The model is instantiated for the Hawkesbury floodplain in Greater Western Sydney and evaluated under small-, medium-, and large-scale scenarios derived from representative flood extents. Computational experiments indicate that optimized volunteer coordination can reduce reliance on expensive outsourcing while maintaining timely coverage of priority regions, and sensitivity analyses highlight that increased volunteer availability and lower outsourcing costs yield the largest improvements in overall performance.

title: An adaptive sparse Bayesian neural network-informed incremental prediction method for remaining useful life of rolling bearings
abstract: The high prediction accuracy of deep neural network (DNN) relies on abundant high-quality training data. However, the remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of bearings is confronted with scarce failure data and poor degradation consistency, which severely restrict the generalization ability of DNN models and the reliability of prediction results. To address this issue, this paper proposes an adaptive sparse Bayesian neural network-informed incremental prediction method for rolling element bearings. Specifically, a temporal cascaded Bayesian neural network framework is designed through the collaborative coupling of Bayesian probabilistic modeling and temporal cascaded network structure, thereby enabling quantitative characterization of prediction uncertainty while capturing the dynamic degradation trend of bearings. Aiming at the widespread issue of high complexity of BNN models, an importance-guided parameter preservation mechanism is constructed to retain parameters encoding professional knowledge while pruning redundant network components for explicit model lightweighting. At the incremental prediction stage, a stage-adaptive correlation alignment strategy is developed to dynamically learn the intrinsic knowledge correlations between different stages, thus alleviating degradation inconsistency issues and improving the model’s generalization and robustness. Experimental results on two test benches indicate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and excellent generalization ability, while comparative experiments with several state-of-the-art methods further validate its robustness and superiority.

title: Interpretable deep learning framework for urban bus traffic safety situation forecast
abstract: Accurate forecasting of urban bus traffic safety is essential for transportation authorities to plan traffic systems, formulate safety policies, and promote public transit use. However, the current understanding of the evolutionary patterns and correlation mechanisms of bus traffic safety with operation-related factors remains limited.​ Thus, this study proposes an Adaptive Three-Stage Temporal Feature Forecasting(ATS-TFF) framework. Taking a mountainous Chinese city as an example, it forecasts the trend of urban bus traffic safety situation (BTSS) and analyzes the relationships between BTSS and multiple influencing factors.​ The results reveal at the feature level, factors such as the mean number of downstream bus stops in the road sections, the mean number of tunnels allowing lane changes along the routes, and the maximum temperature all have substantial effects on BTSS. Temporally, BTSS most significantly affects itself five days later. At the interaction level, the mean number of downstream bus stops in the passed road sections four days prior has the most important impacts on BTSS. ​Overall, the proposed ATS-TFF framework and findings provide data-driven support for proactive bus system safety management, advancing the shift from reactive control to forward-looking, targeted intervention strategies.

title: Physics-informed neural network-based reliability analysis of buried pipelines subjected to permanent ground displacement
abstract: • PINN-RA integrates physics-informed neural networks with Monte Carlo simulation • Extended PINN-based surrogate model solves parametric differential equations of buried pipelines • Uncertainties in soil properties and ground movement magnitude incorporated directly into the model • Ground movement magnitude identified as the dominant factor in reliability assessment • PINN-RA delivers substantial computational efficiency over FEM and FDM methods . Buried pipelines transporting oil and gas across geohazard-prone regions are exposed to potential ground movement, leading to the risk of significant strain demand and structural failure. Reliability analysis, which determines the probability of failure after accounting for pertinent uncertainties, is essential for ensuring the safety of pipeline systems. However, traditional reliability analysis methods involving computationally intensive numerical models, such as finite element simulations of pipelines subjected to ground movement, have limited applications; this is partly because stochastic sampling approaches require repeated simulations over a large number of samples when estimating low probabilities. This study introduces Physics-Informed Neural Network for Reliability Analysis (PINN-RA) for buried pipelines subjected to horizontal permanent ground movement, integrating a PINN-based surrogate model with Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) to achieve efficient reliability assessment.
