To enable its application under uncertain variables associated with soil properties and ground movement, the PINN-based surrogate model is extended to solve a parametric differential equation system, namely the governing equation of pipelines embedded in soil with different properties. The findings demonstrate that PINN-RA significantly reduces the computational effort required and thus accelerates reliability analysis for pipelines subjected to ground movement, enabling rapid decision-making in geohazard-prone regions.

title: Plug-and-play graph reliability enhancement method for equipment state description under sparse information
A dynamic joint predictive maintenance strategy integrating machine degradation and product quality
Data-driven co-design of power distribution networks for resilience enhancement through graph neural network aided performance estimation
abstract: To enhance the resilience of critical infrastructures, a co-design optimization framework is developed for the design of the distribution network and its recovery scheduling. Since network representations are distinct from conventional numerical data, the framework needs to be tailored to overcome unique challenges. Due to the networks being represented as graphs rather than numerical values, derivative-free optimization is the most suitable option. In a random search, the neighborhood must be defined considering the graph data structure. In this study, a surrogate model that can estimate the resilience of the network system is built using a deep-learning-based graph neural network (GNN) to reduce the computational burden during a derivative-free optimization algorithm. Network vulnerabilities are identified using centrality measures from graph theory, where the total demand loss is quantified with sequential component removals to represent resilience loss. Integrating the design optimization to the recovery problem defined as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model, the proposed framework can find the optimum solution for network design and recovery resource scheduling. To prove the efficacy of the proposed GNN-based co-design framework, it was applied for a power system benchmark, where the results demonstrated the practicality of the framework.

title: Identification of key risk factors for unmanned aerial vehicle accidents based on common cause failure Bayesian network
Reliability modeling of fault propagation in software-hardware coupled intelligent ship systems using Petri nets and embedded dynamic Bayesian networks
abstract: Maritime autonomous surface ships are increasingly recognized as complex cyber-physical systems, where autonomous navigation depends on tightly coupled software and hardware components. Conventional reliability assessment approaches often assume independence between software and hardware, which limits their accuracy in capturing fault propagation mechanism. This paper proposes a novel reliability modeling framework that explicitly incorporates software-hardware coupling. First, Fault propagation paths are represented using Petri Nets (PN) to capture dynamic interactions among components. The PN structure is then transformed into an embedded Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN), enabling dynamic probabilistic reasoning over fault dependencies. By integrating PNs with DBNs, a coupled reliability model is constructed for intelligent ship autonomous navigation systems. A case study on an autonomous navigation task demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in quantifying system reliability, identifying critical software and hardware components, and highlighting fault propagation effects that are overlooked in a decoupled model. The results confirm that the proposed approach enhances both the accuracy and interpretability of reliability assessment for intelligent ship systems.

title: Time-varying cause tracing-supplemented risk prediction framework for wind turbines under complex uncertain conditions
Joint optimisation of dynamic quality monitoring and maintenance strategy with quality and degradation considerations
How rescuers’ movement patterns affect emergency evacuation in corridors
Risk emergence mechanism based on quantum mechanics and application in battery management systems
A two-stage resilient restoration framework for large-scale urban electric infrastructure systems under extreme hurricane disasters considering social vulnerability and economic factors
Topic mining and evolution analysis of civil aircraft operational risk factors: A novel domain-adapted BERTopic framework
Identifying influential nodes in social networks for risk management: A dynamic game approach
InSight-R: A structured interface data-driven framework for dynamic human reliability analysis of interface-induced errors
abstract: Human-machine interface (HMI) failures remain a major contributor to human errors in safety-critical systems, yet conventional human reliability analysis (HRA) largely relies on qualitative judgment. Although recent cognitive modeling approaches introduce quantitative mechanisms, they rarely link objective interface design attributes directly to human error probabilities in dynamic operational contexts. To address this gap, we propose InSight-R, a structured interface data-driven probabilistic framework that quantitatively models the association between interface design attributes and interface-induced human errors. By integrating objective interface analytics, empirical behavioral data, and hierarchical probabilistic inference, the framework enables path-level diagnosis of interface-induced risks. The model captures theoretically motivated directional relationships between interface metrics and operator cognitive-behavioral states, where target salience, semantic interference, and interaction span jointly predict execution-related and time-deviation errors. The framework was evaluated on a high-fidelity nuclear simulator using representative panel-inspection tasks with licensed operators and student participants. Results show that increased visual and semantic complexity is associated with higher probabilities of execution errors and temporal deviations. By establishing a quantitative link between interface design attributes and human error probabilities, InSight-R provides a data-driven refinement of HMI-related performance shaping factors and supports dynamically interpretable human reliability analysis.

title: Optimal allocation of time redundancy and abort policies for multiple sequential tasks
Reliability of a multi-state cold chain distribution network with quality loss and quantity loss
Interactive Data–Knowledge Synergy via Guidance and Feedback for Railway Risk Decision-Making
Active learning Kriging with spherical low-discrepancy sampling and gradient refinement for efficient reliability analysis of geotechnical systems
abstract: Reliability analysis of geotechnical systems often requires numerous high-fidelity simulations to evaluate complex limit state functions (LSFs), resulting in prohibitive computational cost. Traditional surrogate-based approaches, such as active learning Kriging with Monte Carlo simulation (AK-MCS), often suffer from local clustering of background samples and inefficient exploration of the failure domain, especially in high-dimensional problems. To address these limitations, an enhanced active learning Kriging framework, termed AK-SLDS, is developed. The method integrates a spherical low-discrepancy sampling (SLDS) scheme with a gradient-refined learning strategy to improve the global representativeness of background samples and the local accuracy of surrogate updates. The performance of AK-SLDS is verified through five numerical examples, including two benchmark problems and three engineering applications. The two benchmark problems demonstrate the method’s accuracy and efficiency for low- to medium-dimensional reliability analyses. The engineering examples, involving the bearing capacity of a shallow footing and two slope stability problems, confirm its robustness for strongly nonlinear and high-dimensional geotechnical systems. Results show that AK-SLDS produces failure probability estimates in close agreement with MCS while requiring substantially fewer true LSF evaluations compared with conventional active learning approaches. The method thus provides an efficient and reliable framework for conducting reliability analysis in geotechnical systems.

title: Active learning with dynamic exploitation-exploration balance for aircraft engine remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for aircraft engines using deep learning is often hindered by the scarcity of labeled run-to-failure data. Active learning (AL) addresses this by selecting the most informative samples for labeling, but traditional methods often use fixed criteria and fail to properly balance the exploitation-exploration trade-off. This paper proposes a novel AL framework that dynamically manages this balance. We utilize a Bayesian hybrid deep learning model to quantify prognostic uncertainty. Based on this, we develop a dual-criteria acquisition function, which integrates uncertainty and diversity by using a feedback mechanism to dynamically adjust their balance. To mitigate redundancy in batch queries, we also introduce a greedy selection algorithm to promote intra-batch diversity. Validation on the C-MAPSS and PHM08 benchmark datasets demonstrates that our framework achieves high RUL prediction accuracy with significantly fewer labeled samples than the compared AL strategies.

title: Gateway placement optimization for cascading survivability enhancement in low earth orbit satellite networks
Post-earthquake functionality and patient waiting times of fully equipped hospital critical rooms using 3D virtual reality damage scenarios
abstract: Lately, hospital functionality has been significantly reduced or halted due to the severity of the earthquake-induced nonstructural damage occurred within their critical rooms. Furthermore, there is a lack of methodologies and models that realistically simulate loss of functionality. Aiming to address this knowledge gap, this research assesses the Residual Functionality (RF) and patient Waiting Times (WT) of hospital critical rooms. To this end, an Emergency Room (ER), an Intensive Care Unit (ICU), and an Operating Room (OR) are simulated at the first, fourth, and fifth levels, respectively, of a mid-rise hospital building, considering Fixed-to-the-Base (FB) and Base-Isolated (BI) support conditions. Both buildings are subjected to Service (SE), Design (DE), and Maximum Considered Earthquake (MCE) levels. Cutting-edge 3D virtual reality (3D-VR) damage scenarios of these rooms are developed from probabilistic damage scenarios considering the structural, nonstructural, and content interactions simultaneously. Next, a hybrid approach that combines the 3D-VR damage scenarios with expert elicitation is adopted to obtain physician expert judgments on RF and WT. These assessments are then used to develop RF and WT fragility curves using Monte Carlo simulations. Fragility results indicate that for the DE level and BI support condition, the ER, ICU, and OR will lose 4%, 3%, and 11% of their functionality, respectively, whereas for the FB support condition, these rooms will lose 30%, 42%, and 70% of their functionality, respectively. Additionally, under BI conditions, these rooms will experience WTs of 28, 16, and 11 minutes, respectively, while for the FB support condition, they will undergo WTs of about 2, 5, and 3 hours, respectively.

title: Stochastic functional resilience assessment and heuristic recovery modeling of urban transportation networks subjected to earthquakes
A hierarchical imprecise probability approach to reliability assessment of large language models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across diverse domains, raising the need for rigorous reliability assessment methods. Existing benchmark-based evaluations primarily offer descriptive statistics of model accuracy over datasets, providing limited insight into the probabilistic behavior of LLMs under real operational conditions. This paper introduces HIP-LLM, a H ierarchical I mprecise P robability framework for modeling and inferring LLM reliability. Building upon the foundations of software reliability engineering, HIP-LLM defines LLM reliability as the probability of failure-free operation over a specified number of future tasks under a given Operational Profile (OP). HIP-LLM represents dependencies across (sub-)domains hierarchically, enabling multi-level inference from subdomain to system-level reliability. HIP-LLM embeds imprecise priors to capture epistemic uncertainty and incorporates OPs to reflect usage contexts. It derives posterior reliability envelopes that quantify uncertainty across priors and data. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that HIP-LLM offers a more nuanced and standardized reliability characterization than existing benchmark and state-of-the-art approaches. A publicly accessible repository of HIP-LLM is provided.

title: Development of a life-cycle risk-based integrity management model for offshore pipelines subjected to corrosion-impact combined loads, embracing high uncertainties and non-linearities
System safety risk assessment of urban tunnel diverging areas under coupled geometric complexity and traffic demand: A driving simulator study
Decision support impact and error prediction in control room: A behavioural data analysis
abstract: Data from psychophysiological measures can offer new insight into control room operators’ behaviour, cognition, and mental workload status. This is particularly helpful when assessing capacity to respond to critical plant conditions such as alarm response scenarios. However, wearable tools such as eye tracking and electroencephalography caps can be perceived as intrusive and unsuitable for daily operations. Therefore, this article examines the potential of using real-time data from process and operator-system interactions during abnormal scenarios, recorded and retrieved from the distributed control system’s historian or process log, to provide insight into operator behaviour and predict their response outcomes without intruding on daily tasks. Data for this study were obtained from a design of experiment using a formaldehyde production plant simulator and four human-in-the-loop support configurations. A comparison between configurations in terms of both behaviour and performance is presented. Then, a step-wise logistic regression and a Bayesian network model were used to predict operator error. The results identified predictive metrics, discussed in terms of their value as precursors of overall system performance in alarm response scenarios. Knowledge of relevant and predictive behavioural metrics accessible in real time can better equip decision-makers to predict outcomes and provide timely support measures for operators.

title: Exploring the robustness of intercity transportation network under typhoon disasters with cascading failures
Optimizing offshore wind farm maintenance with a robust busy period queuing model under natural hazards
Can index-based weather insurance enhance the sustainability of renewable electricity systems? A game-theoretic analysis
What are the composition patterns of critical link combinations for enhancing road network redundancy?
Stochastic-based framework for comparing risk estimates of multi-span masonry arch bridges subject to seismic and flood hazards
abstract: Railway networks are highly centralized and operate as series systems, where failure of a single component, e.g. , bridges, can disrupt the entire line. Masonry arch bridges (MABs) account for approximately 40% of the bridge stock in many European railway networks and often exceed their design operational life. Their vulnerability can increase significantly when exposed to natural hazards, particularly for larger and slender multi-span configurations susceptible to global out-of-plane failure mode. Therefore, quantifying and comparing the multi-hazard vulnerability of these assets is essential to identify critical infrastructure. This research proposes a risk-based framework for assessing out-of-plane failure of multi-span MABs under seismic and flood hazards. The framework employs stochastic surrogate models to derive fragility surfaces directly in the hazard domain without assuming log-normality. Joint hazard probabilities are used to account for asset exposure, considering peak ground acceleration and flow discharge as intensity measures for seismic and flood hazards, respectively. The resulting risk curves support the prioritization of infrastructure assets across hazard-intensity levels. The framework is demonstrated by comparing monetary risk estimates for two multi-span MABs identified as critical infrastructure in the Portuguese railway network.

title: A cell-to-system cross-domain health prognostics framework incorporating adaptive step-size decomposition and noise uncertainty
A data-driven framework for failure probability prediction of water supply pipelines: Integrating feature selection and homogeneous grouping
abstract: Accurate prediction of water supply pipeline failure probability over a future period is vital for risk prevention. Within the prediction period, pipeline failures are typically modeled as a Poisson process. Nonetheless, the scarcity and poor quality of historical failure data necessitate homogeneous grouping to estimate average failure rates. A key challenge in this process is determining how to select appropriate features for grouping, as it directly affects prediction accuracy. This study proposes a data-driven framework integrating feature selection and homogeneous grouping to improve failure probability prediction. First, failure observation samples for a specific time period are generated based on the pipeline’s failure records. A layered feature selection strategy combining filter and wrapper methods is designed to balance selection efficiency with model performance. Filter methods are used to identify candidate feature subsets based on correlation with failure rates. These subsets are then used for grouping, resulting in multiple failure probability labeled datasets. For each, prediction models are developed using Artificial Neural Network and Support Vector Regression. The optimal feature subset and corresponding model are determined by comparing predictive performance. The framework’s effectiveness is validated using a case study of water supply pipelines in the central area of Shanghai, China.

title: Fast charging shock-nonlinear degradation coupled model for battery remaining useful life prediction
Active learning reliability analysis of highly non-stationary geotechnical systems using adaptive compressive sensing-enhanced Kriging and Monte Carlo simulation
abstract: Kriging has been widely used to develop active learning methods for improving the efficiency of reliability analysis, owing to its capability to provide both response prediction and uncertainty quantification. However, conventional Kriging methods rely on the assumption of stationarity, limiting their effectiveness in interpolating non-stationary data. To address this challenge, this study develops an innovative active learning method using adaptive compressive sensing (CS)-enhanced Kriging (ACSK) and Monte Carlo simulation (MCS), termed ACSK-MCS, for reliability analysis of highly non-stationary geotechnical systems. In ACSK-MCS, a novel CS-enhanced Kriging response surface method (RSM) is first proposed by employing a non-parametric CS approach based on discrete cosine transform basis functions to construct the non-stationary trend function. It incorporates both the advantage of Bayesian compressive sensing-based RSM in accurately modeling highly non-stationary response surface from sparse sampling data, and the exact interpolation capability of Kriging-based RSM, thereby enabling a powerful active learning capability. Subsequently, CS-enhanced Kriging RSM is integrated with a learning function to adaptively determine the minimum number of sampling points required and their corresponding locations for achieving the target accuracy of reliability analysis. Numerical investigations on three highly non-stationary analytical benchmark examples and an engineering application demonstrate the effectiveness of ACSK-MCS.

title: An integrated risk assessment framework for multimodal transportation systems: fusing rule-augmented Bayesian networks with personalized individual semantics
abstract: • Proposes an integrated ISM-PIS-RABN framework for full-cycle risk assessment of multimodal transportation systems. • Introduces personalized individual semantics to quantify expert heterogeneous, mitigating group decision bias. • Employs rule-augmented Bayesian networks with factor decomposition to overcome the curse of dimensionality. • Validated via a real-world corridor case, providing actionable insights from sensitivity analysis. Multimodal transportation plays a pivotal role in international trade and logistics due to its unparalleled advantages in cost, efficiency, sustainability, and accessibility. However, its complex structure, which is characterized by multiple transfer points, long transit times, and extended routes, makes it more prone to risks than unimodal transport. Conducting scientific risk assessment and identifying critical factors are essential for improving safety. Therefore, this study proposes a risk assessment model integrating Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM), Personalized Individual Semantics (PIS), and a Rule-Augmented Bayesian Network (RABN), forming a systematic framework covering risk factors identification, correlation analysis, and comprehensive evaluation. Potential risk factors affecting multimodal transport safety are first identified from a 4M1E (Man, Machine, Material, Management, Environment) perspective. ISM is then used to classify these factors hierarchically and construct the Bayesian network structure. By combining PIS, similarity measures, and Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW), the model processes expert judgments to determine root node probabilities. Finally, RABN performs probabilistic inference for risk assessment. The proposed framework is validated through a case study on a route in the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor. Sensitivity analysis further identifies key risk factors and verifies parameter robustness, offering decision-making support for multimodal transportation risk management.

title: Unified stochastic modeling and reliability assessment for coupled degradation mechanisms
Reliability modeling of systems under dependent competing failures using bilateral coupling variables
Post-earthquake functionality assessment and emergency base station deployment optimization for communication systems
A Bayesian uncertainty-guided transfer learning method for trustworthy fault diagnosis of rotating components
abstract: The overall reliability and safety of mission-critical equipment, such as aero-engines, largely depend on the health of their rotating parts. Therefore, trustworthy fault diagnosis is essential for achieving reliability-centered health management. Existing methods face several challenges under cross-working conditions, including computational redundancy, a high risk of negative transfer, and a lack of awareness of uncertainty. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel trustworthy fault diagnosis method based on transfer learning. More specifically, first, a domain-shared feature encoder that fuses sparse self-attention and a deep CNN is designed to extract local and global features. Second, a Bayesian classifier based on variational inference is constructed and combined with Monte Carlo sampling to quantify epistemic uncertainty. Then, a domain alignment mechanism combining explicit and implicit discrepancy measures is introduced. Meanwhile, the uncertainty is mapped via an exponential decay function into adaptive weights that guide domain alignment, thereby prioritizing the transfer of high-confidence samples and suppressing unreliable ones. Finally, the experimental results on the gear dataset show that the proposed method achieved the highest accuracy rate of 99.11% in three transfer tasks. Moreover, among the correct predictions, 91.84% fall within the low-uncertainty region, while all misclassifications are flagged as high-uncertainty. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can provide trustworthy, uncertainty-aware diagnostics to enhance the reliability and safety of complex mechanical systems.

title: A framework for load effect combination considering spatiotemporal uncertainty of multiple loads
Risk-evolution forecasting of epidemic transmission with physics-informed neural networks for a modified susceptible–infected–quarantined–recovered–susceptible model
abstract: Epidemic transmission involves nonlinear mechanisms, heterogeneous contacts, and multiple delays, which challenges conventional approaches to balance mechanistic fidelity and predictive accuracy. An integrated framework is developed by coupling a modified Susceptible–Infected–Quarantined–Recovered–Susceptible compartmental model with physics-informed neural networks. The model introduces an adaptive nonlinear incidence function and dual delay mechanisms, including incubation delay and decision-to-quarantine delay. The basic reproduction number is derived analytically via the next-generation matrix method, with stability proofs for both disease-free and endemic equilibria. A physics-informed neural-network-based inverse-problem solver is constructed to infer latent states and time-varying parameters by minimizing a composite objective that penalizes both data mismatch and equation residuals, while uncertainty is assessed through repeated training under perturbed observations. Numerical experiments examine how alternative delay values reshape epidemic outcomes, including final size, peak magnitude, and outbreak duration, thereby clarifying the distinct transmission pathways regulated by each delay. Validation with early-phase empirical data from the Wuhan coronavirus disease 2019 outbreak indicates that the framework yields accurate reconstruction of time-varying parameters and reliable short-term trend forecasting, supporting risk-informed decision making and safety evaluation in epidemic scenarios.

title: Impact of integrating intermittent renewable energy on the reliability of Morocco's power system through 2030
Generative data-physics fusion for hierarchical reliability assessment
Resilient ventilation network construction in complex underground mining environments: A holistic strategy from resilience perception to resilience enhancement
Reliability analysis and update for internet of things systems considering cross-layer dependencies
A correlation-aligned proxy-learning framework for few-shot prediction of battery remaining useful life
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for quantifying battery operational safety and longevity, yet the deployment of machine learning techniques is often constrained by a widespread deficiency of high-quality labelled degradation data. To address this challenge, we propose a correlation-aligned proxy-learning framework that establishes a principled bridge between scarce RUL labels and opportunistic ageing cues. The framework employs a bilateral-branch neural network to explicitly disentangle initial manufacturing variability from in-use degradation dynamics, ensuring robust feature extraction across heterogeneous cells. By recasting a class of differential incremental capacity (ΔIC)-based descriptors as proxy labels, the method leverages their strong intra-cell and through-life correlation with RUL to transform the under-determined few-shot regression problem into a consistency-matching task. This strategy effectively constrains the model’s learning manifold, enabling the exploitation of non-ideal indicators from routine charging events while mitigating the risk of overfitting. Validated across diverse battery chemistries and cycling temperatures, the framework significantly outperforms conventional semi-supervised baselines, delivering more than a 50% improvement in prediction accuracy under extreme few-shot regimes.

title: Virtual sensing by grey-box modelling within an importance sampling Monte Carlo dynamic event tree framework for risk monitoring of small modular reactors
abstract: Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) integrate advanced safety features. However, the compactness of their core design renders it difficult to position measurement devices, for operation and risk monitoring. To address this issue, we develop a Grey-Box (GB) modelling framework that ensembles White-Box (WB) physics-based and Black-Box (BB) data-driven models to enable virtual sensing of in-core safety-critical variables. The BB model is trained with condition monitoring data to perform multi-step ahead estimation of measurable variables; the estimates are fed to a physics-based WB model to estimate the non-measurable variables. The GB model developed is embedded within a risk monitoring module that builds on an Importance Sampling Monte Carlo Dynamic Event Tree (IS-MCDET) to provide the risk profile of the SMR. The method is tested on the Small Modular Dual Fluid Reactor (SMDFR), a new-generation SMR whose developed GB model for risk monitoring consists in a zero-dimensional Thermal Hydraulic (TH) WB model and a Bi-directional Long-Short Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) BB model. The developed GB model is shown to comply with the regulatory requirements and explainable response to support risk-informed decision making.
keywords: Importance sampling Monte Carlo dynamic event tree (IS-MCDET)

title: Intelligent early warning and adaptive regulation of symbiotic risks in the energy metal supply chain: A critical slowing down perspective
Failure mode identification for dynamic stochastic systems using operator norm and parameter space sample search
Reliability evaluation and optimization for a redundant repairable cluster computing system
Joint optimization of condition-based maintenance and product quality improvement for deteriorating manufacturing systems in a random environment
An integrated Bayesian framework for aircraft performance evaluation from segmented flight tests
Spatially cascading failure analysis in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei hydrogen energy industry Chain: A multilayer network approach
Development of urban fire risk index based on fire damage weighting methodologies and AI analysis of meteorological factors
abstract: As urban density increases, the development of reliable quantitative indicators for fire risk assessment becomes essential for disaster management. However, existing studies have tended to rely on single weighting methods without validating their suitability for predictive modeling based on meteorological conditions. This study constructed fire risk indices using three distinct methodologies: principal component analysis (PCA) for statistical objectivity, analytic hierarchy process (AHP) for expert judgment, and value of statistical life (VSL) for economic valuation. Using ten years of fire and meteorological data from Busan, risk grades were classified using K-Means clustering, and predictive models were developed via a Random Forest (RF) classifier based on four key meteorological variables (average temperature, maximum wind speed, effective humidity, and sea-level pressure). Comparative analysis revealed that the AHP and VSL models, which placed excessive weight on fatalities, showed low correlation with meteorological conditions and poor predictive performance for high-risk events (recall < 0.20). In contrast, the PCA-based index effectively captured the physical mechanisms of fire spread under low temperature, dry, and high-pressure conditions. The PCA model achieved a precision and recall of 0.99 in classifying high-risk grades. While AHP and VSL are useful for post-event impact assessment, this study demonstrated that the PCA-based index is the most scientifically valid and reliable measure for a meteorology-based predictive early warning system.

title: Optimal aborting and performance policy in resource constrained missions with phase dependent cost of system failure
Enhancing car-following risk prediction reliability: A noise-robust mixture of experts framework
Optimizing fault tree traversal order for efficient minimal cut set generation: A lightweight graph neural network approach
abstract: Although the downward method is widely used in fault tree analysis, the critical impact of sibling node traversal order on computational efficiency has received insufficient attention. Current approaches rely on either fixed heuristic rules or random selection, resulting in unstable computational performance. To address this challenge, we introduce graph neural networks to intelligently optimize node traversal order. We construct a comprehensive dataset that maps graph structures and node orderings to computational costs, and propose a novel two-stage training framework: a cost prediction network that evaluates ordering quality, followed by a ranking generator guided by predicted costs. Experimental evaluation on industrial fault trees demonstrates that our GNN-based approach consistently identifies efficient traversal strategies, achieving 1.5–40 × speedups over conventional methods and competitive performance against established solvers. By transforming the discrete combinatorial optimization problem into a learnable task, this work provides a new perspective for optimizing topological traversal in minimal cut set analysis.

title: An efficient adaptive multi-fidelity ensemble of surrogates method for structural reliability analysis
Stress-coupled parameter learning in stochastic processes for reliability-oriented accelerated degradation modeling
abstract: Accelerated degradation testing is widely used for reliability assessment, yet stochastic processes cannot be directly utilized to model accelerated degradation data because they lack inherent stress covariate. To address this problem, the stress-coupled parameters, whose values vary with stress levels, must first be determined. Then, the stress-coupled parameters are replaced by acceleration models to construct a degradation model incorporating stress covariate. However, the assumed stress-coupled parameters have commonly been adopted, resulting in poor explicability of accelerated degradation modeling and unreliable life extrapolation results, particularly when multiple assumptions on stress-coupled parameters exist for a given degradation model. This study proposes an explicable framework for determining stress-coupled parameters in stochastic processes. The framework consists of two approaches: an analytical derivation method for linear degradation models and a numerical computation method for nonlinear models. These approaches are applied to Wiener, Gamma, and Inverse Gaussian processes to derive stress-coupled parameters, validating the equivalence of them for linear degradation models and revealing that different time functions fundamentally determine the stress-dependency patterns of model parameters. The numerical computation method is applicable to complex degradation models, but it can not discover the potential proportional relationship among multiple stress-coupled parameters. To address this issue, the framework offers a workflow combining the two approaches. A case study on electrical connectors further verifies the practical effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results show that the framework works well in deriving stress-coupled parameters and benefits strengthening the theoretical basis of accelerate degradation modeling.

title: Energy-saving optimization of train speed Profile based on online Policy deep reinforcement learning algorithm under emergency conditions
abstract: In the domain of energy-efficient train-speed-profile optimization, off-policy reinforcement-learning (RL) algorithms and their variants have long dominated the academic landscape. Such approaches typically rely on an experience-replay buffer to reuse historical samples, yet they suffer from low training efficiency, poor numerical stability, and insufficient real-time responsiveness—limitations that become critical in complex metro systems or under emergency conditions. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose an on-policy RL framework termed the Energy-Saving Maximization Advantage Distribution (ES-MAD) algorithm. ES-MAD abandons the replay buffer and instead employs dual policy networks (new vs. old): data collected by the newly explored policy are immediately leveraged to update the old policy, thereby markedly improving sample efficiency. In addition, a normalized-and-scaled advantage function is introduced to reduce variance, which significantly enhances model stability in highly dynamic or emergency scenarios. Finally, a multi-objective, self-adaptive reward mechanism is designed that seamlessly integrates energy efficiency, punctuality, ride comfort, and stopping accuracy; this reward structure requires no re-tuning when the system switches between normal and emergency operating modes. Experimental validation on the Yizhuang metro line demonstrates that ES-MAD exhibits strong robustness and generalization capability under regular service, sudden schedule changes, and multi-interval comprehensive tests. Compared with state-of-the-art off-policy deep RL baselines, ES-MAD achieves 24 % and 26 % additional energy-saving under normal and emergency conditions, respectively.

title: Distributionally robust bi-level optimization for reliability management of medical waste reverse logistics network under uncertainty
Batch active learning for reliability-based model validation
abstract: In engineering, quantifying the deviation between model prediction and reality is crucial, particularly when simulation or empirical models are used in safety-critical applications or for product release. Model validation aims to quantify this discrepancy by comparing model predictions to experimental results. However, conducting physical experiments for validation is often costly and time-consuming. Active learning strategies can mitigate this problem by reducing the data needed to assess model accuracy. In practice, these strategies must account for experimental uncertainties, such as material variability. This work proposes an active learning framework for model validation focused on efficiently identifying the limit state between valid and invalid model regions under such conditions. Therefore, we introduce a decision-theoretical basis from which we derive two novel misclassification-based acquisition functions for mean-based and quantile-based validation. Furthermore, the framework is extended to the batch setting, allowing multiple points to be proposed for evaluation while considering nonlinear constraints of the input space. The proposed method is compared to alternative approaches for several analytical and engineering problems. Finally, the validation of a temperature model for an electric motor demonstrates the efficiency of the method in a complex scenario.

Dynamic propagation and control strategies of environmental, social, and governance risks in international digital infrastructure development

Maintenance planning for nonlinearly degrading systems: a reliability-constrained non-periodic inspection strategy

Distribution networks scheduling with multiple flexibility resources under earthquake scenarios considering decision-dependent uncertainty
Optimal inspection timing in missions with expected profit-based abort policy

Integrated simulation and network analysis of battery fire risk in underground mining systems

Reliability assessment of a multi-response bridge system considering climate change effects on wind and wave loads
abstract: This study proposes a novel reliability analysis framework to efficiently evaluate the long-term reliability of multi-response structures under climate change. In this framework, an error-controlled multi-input-multi-output surrogate model is developed based on a support vector regression method, which can propagate uncertainties of structural parameters to responses with satisfactory accuracy while minimising computational costs. By integrating the copula theory and reliability assessment method, the multi-response failure probability is derived, considering both correlations between responses and uncertainties of performance thresholds. In addition, future data on wind climate are collected to account for climate change, and a neural network model is trained using historical and simulated data to predict future wave heights. The framework is then applied to a long-span cable-stayed and suspension bridge system as a case study. Analysis results demonstrate that a comprehensive multi-responses reliability analysis, which considers correlations between responses, can reflect the overall fragility of structures and prevent the underestimation of structural risk. Though the trends in structural failure probabilities vary depending on the climate model, climate change significantly influences structural risk assessment. This study provides a novel perspective for the structural reliability assessment of complex structures.

title: A k-GNN Wiener process interactive RUL prognosis method for stochastic degrading devices monitored by related multiple sensors
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for making proactive decisions regarding the health management activities of degrading devices, thereby effectively ensuring safe, reliable, and economic operations. For degrading devices monitored by multiple sensors, hybrid prognosis methods combining statistical-model-based and deep-learning-based approaches, have become popular in the field of prognostics and health management. However, existing studies based on open-loop model architectures, tend to overlook the correlations and complementary relationships among multiple sensors, leading to a reduction in prediction accuracy. Therefore, this paper presents a novel data-model integrative prognosis framework incorporating high-order graph neural networks (GNNs) and Wiener process (WP). Specifically, a k-order GNN (k-GNN) capturing the high-order interaction information among different sensors is utilized to construct a composite health index (CHI). Subsequently, the time-varying stochastics within the CHI is depicted through a WP. By joint learning parameters of the k-GNN with those of the WP, a closed-loop framework is established to improve the matching degree between the constructed CHI and the WP-based degradation models. Both experimental results on simulated datasets including C-MAPSS and N-CMAPSS and real-world case study results on milling cutter dataset demonstrate that the proposed k-GNN-WP model achieves a substantial improvement in RUL prediction accuracy.

title: Resilience patterns in higher-order meta-population networks
abstract: Meta-population networks are effective tools for capturing population movement across distinct regions, but the assumption of well-mixed regions fails to capture the reality of population higher-order interactions. As a multidimensional system capturing mobility characteristics, meta-population networks are inherently complex and difficult to interpret when subjected to resilience analysis based on N-dimensional equations. We propose a higher-order meta-population model that captures large-scale global cross-regional mobility and small-scale higher-order interactions within regions. Remarkably, we extend the dimension-reduction approach, simplifying the N-dimensional higher-order meta-population system into a one-dimensional equation by decomposing different network behaviours into a single universal resilience function, thereby allowing for convenient and accurate prediction of the system resilience. The network structure and human mobility parameters can clearly and simply express the epidemic threshold. Numerical experimental results on both real networks and star networks confirm the accuracy of the proposed dimension-reduction framework in predicting the evolution of epidemic dynamics on higher-order meta-population networks. Additionally, higher-order interactions among populations are shown to lead to explosive growth in the epidemic infection size potentially. Population mobility causes changes in the spatial distribution of infectious diseases across different regions.

title: A novel event tree analysis-graphical evaluation and review technique network model for comprehensive fault analysis in rocket hydrogen-oxygen refueling
The reliability of remotely piloted aircraft system performance under aeronautical communication uncertainties
abstract: Mission-critical operations of highly maneuverable Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) require reliable communication to ensure safe integration into existing airspace. Understanding system-level performance under stochastic communication conditions is essential for estimating mission success and assessing operational risks. This study quantifies the impact of communication latency and complete signal loss on the mission completion performance of a highly maneuverable RPAS. The mission is defined as a static waypoint tracking task in three-dimensional airspace. We first derive mathematical formulations for key reliability metrics within the Required Communication Performance (RCP) framework. These stochastic communication factors, including latency and availability, are then incorporated into flight control simulations to evaluate system behavior. Extensive multiprocessing Monte Carlo simulations are conducted using high-performance computing to generate mission success rate and mission completion time envelopes. Results show significant degradation in flight performance as communication latency increases or availability decreases, which directly reduces the system stability margin. To better characterize this relationship, we introduce a new reliability metric, communicability, which integrates three key RCP metrics and provides insight into the maximum tolerable latency for flight control. The proposed framework informs RPAS design by revealing trade-offs between communication capability and flight control performance. The code used in this study is publicly available at this \href{https://github.com/YutianPangASU/comm-dynamics}{repository}.

title: Towards AI-Driven smart maintenance of computed tomography equipment: From health indicator design to transferable remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Failures of Computed Tomography (CT) equipment can disrupt hospital operations and compromise patient safety. However, research on Predictive Maintenance (PdM) for such systems remains limited. The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) provides a practical foundation by enabling real-time acquisition of high-dimensional operational data. This study proposes a deep learning framework for predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of CT equipment. First, a physics-guided Health Indicator (HI) is defined as the deviation between the observed current and the predicted nominal current of the X-ray tube filament. Second, a CT-specific degradation path identification module that combines operational state filtering with adaptive signal fusion to extract smooth, physically consistent trends is proposed. Third, a bidirectional LSTM sequence-to-sequence model, combined with cross-equipment transfer learning and uncertainty quantification, is developed for RUL prediction under heterogeneous work states and across different equipment. The framework is validated on real-world IoMT-collected X-ray tube filament datasets from multiple hospitals and CT equipment. The proposed framework achieves prediction errors of 0.3, 3.0, and 2.3 days with error rates of 0.23%, 2.33%, and 1.78%, respectively, outperforming classic and recent strong baselines in temporal alignment and generalization. These results demonstrate the potential of IoMT-enabled PdM to support maintenance decision-making, clinical workflow optimization, and downtime minimization.

title: Data-driven warranty modeling for multi-state deteriorating products with stochastic repair times
abstract: This paper presents a data-driven approach to extracting warranty models for multi-state deteriorating repairable products, with a focus on scenarios involving stochastic repair times. While analytical solutions exist for cases with negligible or fixed repair/replacement durations, no explicit solutions are available when these times are stochastic. To address the lack of explicit solutions for stochastic repair times, we first extract models from failure and repair data, then apply a modified Proxel-based simulation to determine optimal repair-replacement policies that minimize expected warranty servicing costs per item sold. Our results reveal that when minimal repairs are performed instantaneously, replacement is generally favored over early repairs. Conversely, when repair times are non-zero, the system tends to prefer repair over replacement. Additionally, we find that data-driven warranty models evolve with continuous data integration but often underestimate reliability due to biased failure data, highlighting the need for bias-aware modeling techniques.

title: A width-optimized ensemble uncertainty calibration approach for interval reliability analysis
Optimising trade-offs between cyber reliability and cyber-physical risk for water distribution systems
abstract: • Novel analysis of trade-offs between cyber-physical risk and cyber-reliability • Introduction of a practical Cyber Connectivity metric to aid decision making • Application to two cyber-physical water systems, C-Town and Richmond • Novel process to identify redundancy strategies in cyber-physical water systems • Development of an optimisation framework for this risk/reliability trade-off Water distribution systems (WDSs) are critical for human survival. The ability to control these systems remotely via cyber networks has made it possible to increase their functionality significantly. The degree of effectiveness of this control is a function of the reliability of the cyber network (i.e. cyber reliability), which can be increased via the addition of redundant cyber components. However, this also has the potential to reduce WDS reliability by increasing opportunities for cyber-attacks (i.e. increasing cyber physical risk). Consequently, it is imperative to consider the potential trade-off between increasing cyber reliability and decreasing cyber-physical risk in the design of WDSs. In this paper, we introduce novel approaches for quantifying and optimising this trade-off, including a novel cyber-connectivity metric for estimating WDS cyber-physical risk in a practically efficient manner. Application of our approaches to two complex WDSs shows that the degree to which an increase in cyber network reliability increases cyber-physical risk is highly variable, depending on the configuration of the redundant cyber components. This suggests that there are opportunities to design cyber networks in a way that minimises increases in cyber-physical risk for a given increase in cyber reliability. The ability of our proposed optimisation framework to achieve this is demonstrated for the two WDSs considered. While the quantification and optimisation approaches presented in this paper are tailored to WDSs, the underlying principles are also applicable to cyber-physical systems in other problem domains.

title: High-intensity forest fire early warning in fire-prone areas
A novel method for multi-source fusion identification and spatio-temporal probability prediction of settlement target zones along railway lines
Uncertainty-informed cascaded diagnosis of compound faults in electromechanical systems via a physics-informed hypergraph framework
abstract: Compound fault diagnosis is essential for the reliability management and operational safety of complex electromechanical systems. However, existing data-driven methods often treat diagnosis as a flat classification task, failing to capture higher-order physical interdependencies among components and disregarding the cascaded diagnostic logic where system-level health states should logically govern component-level attributions. To address these challenges, we propose an uncertainty-informed cascaded diagnosis framework, which reformulates compound fault diagnosis as a hierarchical reasoning process. The framework first introduces a deterministic Bond-Graph-to-Hypergraph Priors (BG2HP) protocol that converts coarse physical context into two learning-ready priors: a physics-informed hypergraph and a weak constraint set. Building on these priors, a Physics-informed Hypergraph Multi-Task Network (PHG-MTNet) is developed to explicitly model multi-component interactions as higher-order hyperedges and to enforce weak physics consistency through regularization in the latent space. An Uncertainty-informed Cascaded Inference (UCI) strategy is then designed to govern a top-down diagnostic workflow using calibrated predictive uncertainty, efficiently resolving high-confidence system-level syndromes while escalating ambiguous or safety-critical samples to fine-grained component attribution. Validation on a multi-component hydraulic test bench demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves 99.55% accuracy. Ultimately, by providing uncertainty-quantified and physically consistent diagnostic evidence, the proposed framework serves as an actionable and effective tool for optimizing system-wide reliability management and risk-aware maintenance decisions.

title: EPAL: An exponential-penalty based active-learning function for adaptive Kriging models in structural reliability analysis
abstract: Accurate estimation of structural failure probability in engineering systems is frequently limited by the high computational cost of evaluating complex performance functions. This paper introduces an exponential-penalty based active-learning (EPAL) function for adaptive refinement of Kriging models in reliability analysis. The EPAL formulation integrates the Kriging predictive variance with a normalized distance measure relative to the predicted limit-state surface through an exponential decay term. This functional form dynamically suppresses the selection of new samples in regions of low predictive uncertainty or those far from the failure boundary. The inherent resistance to sample clustering ensures a balanced sampling strategy that simultaneously explores regions of high uncertainty and refines the vicinity of the failure boundary. A key feature of this design is that the EPAL function is mathematically simple, parameter-free, and continuously differentiable. By removing the need for empirical tuning parameters or auxiliary distance thresholds, the method reduces subjective bias and computational redundancy. Numerical results from multiple benchmark problems confirm that the proposed method provides accurate failure probability with high computational efficiency. Its effective performance in both engineering applications and problems with small failure events further demonstrates its suitability for reliability analysis involving expensive simulations.

title: Deterministic and probabilistic stability analyses of single tunnel in a cohesive-frictional finite slope
A novel risk assessment framework for piracy threats: mapping system theoretic process analysis and complex network into Bayesian networks
abstract: The enduring nature and complex causes of maritime piracy render incidents nearly inevitable, highlighting the urgent need for effective emergency response mechanisms. To fill this gap, this study develops a novel framework for analyzing anti-piracy emergency response actions from a ship and shore collaborative perspective. Initially, the System-Theoretic Process Analysis approach is employed to identify the intricate causal relationships underlying piracy incidents, which facilitates the systematic construction of a complex network for the anti-piracy emergency response process. To provide a rigorous quantitative basis, a Bayesian Network is established, where node selection is informed by betweenness centrality metrics from the complex network results. Then, three distinct sensitivity analysis methods are introduced to pinpoint critical factors influencing piracy hijacking outcomes. The proposed models are then rigorously verified through cross-model validation and real-world case studies. Our study indicates that the delayed deployment of assets, fatigue-induced inattention, and poor coordination among the crews play critical roles on piracy hijackings risks. This study contributes to a more profound understanding of emergency responses and provides a theoretical foundation for developing effective anti-piracy strategies, thereby enhancing the resilience of the maritime transportation system.

title: Modeling and reliability analysis of cascading failures in asymmetric interdependent hypergraphs
Multimodal operating status prediction for interpretable health assessment of autonomous mining trucks
Quantification of influencing factors in the pedestrian evacuation process under ship motion conditions based on evacuation efficiency analysis
Dynamic functional failure traceability model and diagnosis approach for intelligent manufacturing systems with physics-informed spatiotemporal causal graph
abstract:
ABSTRACT
Functional failure dynamic traceability and reliability assurance have become critical bottlenecks to achieving smart maintenance synergy for intelligent manufacturing systems. Most existing approaches rely on correlation-based statistical monitoring of physical equipment failures, failing to holistically consider the interplay between process parameter deviations and workpiece quality defects during functional failure evolution. This limitation undermines both the accuracy and interpretability of failure diagnosis in complex manufacturing environments. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel Causal Maintenance Control (CMC) framework grounded in the Equipment–Process–Quality (E-P-Q) causal chain. The main contributions are threefold: (1) establishing a dynamic E-P-Q causal chain model that systematically characterizes the cross-process propagation of equipment degradation, parameter deviation, and quality defects in functional failure scenarios; (2) developing a physics-informed spatiotemporal causal graph that integrates thermodynamic constraints, neural differential equations, and process-topology attention to reveal the dynamic causal pathways through which functional failures induce quality anomalies; (3) designing a causal-aware adaptive control framework that combines a two-stage traceability mechanism, a Dynamic Criticality Index (DCI), and constrained Bayesian optimization to achieve real-time root-cause localization and proactive compensation. The proposed approach is validated through an industrial case study of aero-engine turbine blade production line.

title: Scenario dynamics-informed enhancement of power grid resilience to typhoons
Safety evaluation of offshore wind turbine structures based on interval grey relational analysis and combined weighting method
Robust calibration with stochastic emulators: hydrological model parameter estimation under uncertain rainfall conditions
abstract: Traditional calibration methods in hydrological models result in parameter values that can compensate for aleatory uncertainties in model forcings (such as rainfall, temperature, evapotranspiration, or pesticide application dates). Ignoring aleatory uncertainty can lead to subsequent model simulations being less reliable for taking operational decisions or predicting hazardous events (e.g., peaks of water pollution or floods). Robust calibration can better handle these uncertainties, but usually requires extensive model simulations, making it impractical for physically based environmental models. To overcome these issues, we use a new metamodeling approach using stochastic emulation. This method is non-intrusive, meaning it does not need a predefined structure for the forcing space. Once validated, the stochastic emulator is used to evaluate different robust estimators at low cost, allowing for the selection of the most suitable one for the specific problem. We demonstrate this approach using the PESHMELBA hydrological model for pesticide transfer. We construct and validate the stochastic emulator, and compare robust estimators to traditional calibration. Results show that robust calibration enhances the model’s reliability under rainfall uncertainty. This methodology can be applied to any model and forcing uncertainty, making it relevant for other applications in complex technological systems, or environmental models where aleatory uncertainties are inherent.

title: Unification of multi-source and multi-fidelity fragility functions
Towards reliable multimodal disaster severity assessment through preference optimization and explainable vision-language reasoning
abstract: Reliable disaster damage assessment requires models that provide both accurate predictions and transparent explanations. However, existing multimodal approaches are limited by scarce annotated data and insufficient evaluation of reasoning quality. This study proposes a two-stage training framework that integrates Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) within a unified data construction pipeline. From a single Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) annotation workflow, two complementary datasets are derived, namely ReasoningSet, which contains validated rationales for SFT, and PreferenceSet, which comprises paired rationales for DPO-based alignment. The framework evaluates both classification performance and explanation quality using automatic metrics, model-based scoring, and human ranking. Experimental results show that SFT improves accuracy from 73.64% to 78.29% and increases Macro-F1 by 29% compared to the baseline, while explanation quality improves by approximately 25%. Subsequent DPO alignment further enhances interpretability on the PreferenceSet. Cross-model validation on InternVL-3-8B and LLaVA-1.5-7B demonstrates the robustness and generalizability of the approach. The proposed framework improves detection of underrepresented mild damage cases, reduces high-risk misclassifications, and strengthens alignment between model reasoning and human judgment. Overall, it provides a reproducible pathway to develop reliable multimodal systems that deliver auditable, actionable disaster insights for emergency management.

title: Accelerated degradation modeling and reliability assessment method considering random effects and multi-stress time factors
Physics-constrained causal structure learning for root cause analysis in nuclear system monitoring
abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) is important for identifying the initiating cause of faults and analyzing fault propagation paths in nuclear systems. However, robust RCA in nuclear accident monitoring remains challenging because it depends on reliable identification of causal relationships among monitoring variables, which is difficult under complex system coupling and limited-sample conditions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a physics-constrained causal structure learning method for RCA in nuclear accident monitoring. First, a simplified physical model of the nuclear system is constructed to extract a priori causal knowledge among key monitoring variables. Second, the causal relationships among different variables are learned by a score-based causal structure learning method under the guidance of the extracted physical constraints. In this process, physically infeasible edges are excluded and the admissible parent sets are restricted before score optimization. Finally, the root cause nodes of faults are identified based on the learned causal graph. The proposed method is validated using two representative accident scenarios generated from a nuclear simulation platform. The results show that the proposed method can improve root-node identification performance, reduce abnormal-edge misidentification, and enhance the robustness of causal structure learning under limited-sample conditions without introducing additional computational burden.

title: A data-efficient surrogate-based structural reliability approach using a firefly-optimized deep neural network: Application to hang-off drilling riser evacuations
abstract: Reliability assessment of offshore structures subjected to nonlinear hydrodynamic-structural interactions requires uncertainty propagation that is statistically consistent with the full response space. However, fully coupled finite-element (FE) simulations are too computationally expensive for Monte Carlo (MC) analysis, limiting their applicability in nonlinear structural reliability. This study develops a data-efficient structural reliability methodology that integrates nonlinear FE simulations, a firefly-optimized deep neural network (FA-DNN) surrogate model, and MC uncertainty propagation into a unified framework. The methodological innovation lies in the FA-DNN model, where a multi-objective firefly optimization strategy adaptively tunes hyperparameters to improve learning stability, prevent overfitting under limited FE data, and accurately reproduce nonlinear response behavior required for reliability evaluation. Trained on a small FE-generated dataset, the FA-DNN achieves R² values above 0.996 and reduces prediction errors by over 90% compared with ANN and baseline DNN models, enabling fast and statistically consistent MC-based estimation of failure probability. Application to a deepwater riser system in hang-off evacuation serves as a verification example, demonstrating that the methodology yields reliability-informed operational limits with negligible computational cost. The framework is general and transferable, offering an efficient surrogate-enhanced pathway for nonlinear reliability assessment of offshore and other complex structures under stochastic loading.

title: The prediction of limit wheel profile using geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural networks
abstract: Wheel profile prediction is critical to the maintenance of high-speed electric multiple units. This study proposes a geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural network for high-accuracy prediction of worn wheel profiles. A vehicle–track dynamic simulation model is further employed to determine whether predicted worn profiles exceed the limit and to estimate the time-dependent reliability associated with profile degradation. The proposed approach is evaluated via quantitative and qualitative comparisons with a conventional wheelset wear prediction method. Results indicate that the geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural network improves wheel wear prediction accuracy. In addition, the simulation-based prediction is more conservative, and the wear range observed in service is wider than that obtained from simulation. Wear patterns of wheels within the same wheelset also show strong correlations. Moreover, wheel diameter affects wear behaviour, including the wear degradation rate, equivalent conicity, the vehicle critical speed, and the Sperling index. Hence, Maintenance scheduling should therefore account for wheel diameter effects to ensure robust performance and durability.

title: Embracing uncertainty: A review of Bayesian methods for travel time reliability
Bayesian deep learning framework for pesticide transport modeling with uncertainty quantification
abstract: Pesticide transport and transformation in soil pose potential threats to ecological environments and human health, while traditional numerical simulation methods exhibit high computational costs and difficulty in accurately quantifying prediction uncertainty. A Bayesian deep learning framework is developed for pesticide transport modeling, integrating uncertainty quantification, interpretability analysis, and risk assessment. Surrogate models including deterministic, MC Dropout, and Deep Ensemble architectures are constructed based on 447,300 COMSOL simulation data points. The Deep Ensemble model achieves the optimal balance between prediction accuracy (R2>0.96) and uncertainty quantification, with calibration errors of 0.0350–0.0467. SHAP analysis reveals the dominant role of second-layer soil hydraulic parameters, which simultaneously constitute the primary sources of model uncertainty. Spatiotemporal uncertainty analysis shows that the mean prediction uncertainty decreases from 0.21 to 0.05 within 14 days and remains stable at 0.04–0.08 over the full 365-day period.The risk assessment framework reveals that contamination risk escalates from a mean probability of 0.476 (t=2 days) to 0.837 (t=28 days) with 72.1% of the domain classified as very high risk, and the early warning system indicates that the alert and emergency thresholds are triggered at 2.0 and 4.0 days, respectively. Climate change impacts are quantified through 10 scenario analyses: warming reduces the near-surface mean concentration by 18.8% via the Q10 effect, while precipitation changes affect transport through the source concentration (c0) and infiltration forcing (Hp0) pathways, with the c0 pathway dominating most exposure metrics. Under extreme drought conditions, the high-concentration area of aldicarb sulfoxide reaches 20.0–57.2%, far exceeding baseline levels. The framework provides a comprehensive approach to uncertainty-aware pesticide transport prediction, with future extensions needed for three-dimensional heterogeneous systems and multi-pesticide synergistic effects.

title: Physics-Informed Multi-Projection Regression for Roller Bearing Remaining Useful Life Prediction
abstract: Traditional matrix-form data-driven approaches for roller bearing remaining useful life (RUL) prediction suffer from two fundamental challenges, namely the inability to capture the geometric evolution of multi-stage degradation dynamics and the lack of physical consistency under data-scarce conditions. To address these limitations, a novel physics-informed multi-projection regression (PIMPR) model is proposed in this paper, which synergistically integrates physical mechanism priors with a structure-preserving learning framework. First, to bridge the gap between physical mechanisms and data-driven models, a four-degree-of-freedom roller bearing dynamic model incorporating an improved Paris law is constructed. This model characterizes the full-lifecycle degradation process, providing high-fidelity privileged information to guide the learning process. Second, unlike traditional vector-based methods, a structure-preserving matrix regression is introduced to retain the correlation within time-frequency data. Meanwhile, a key novelty is the multi-projection mechanism, which geometrically aligns the data subspaces with the three physical degradation stages, thereby enhancing model interpretability and representation capability. Third, a learning using privileged information paradigm is adopted, where the physically predicted lifespan serves as auxiliary guidance to regularize the training manifold. Comprehensive evaluations on two roller bearing datasets demonstrate the favorable performance of the proposed PIMPR, particularly under data-scarce scenarios.

title: Robustness evaluation method for multi-state combat system-of-systems considering cascading failure
A bivariate Wiener degradation model with partially random scale weights
Analytical resilience assessment and optimization model for large-scale offshore wind farm clusters informed by hourly component-level simulation
A framework for analyzing seismic resilience and chain-reaction economic losses in substations based on sample optimization strategies
Maintenance and reliability optimization of subsea blowout preventer hydraulic systems based on mixed Weibull modeling and redundancy strategies
Bi-level inspection and maintenance policy for a multi-component system subject to dynamic self-reconfiguration
abstract: In multi-component systems, the performance of components may be constrained by the most degraded component, leading to significant performance loss of the system. To mitigate this issue, some systems employ a dynamic self-reconfiguration mechanism that selectively isolates or retrieves components based on their degradation levels, enabling the system to consistently operate at its highest achievable performance. Despite its practical significance, inspection and maintenance optimization for systems subject to dynamic self-reconfiguration remains underexplored, especially in a practical scenario where the system performance can be continuously monitored, while components’ conditions can be revealed only through discrete inspections due to technical or economic constraints. In this study, we propose a bi-level inspection and maintenance policy that integrates system-level monitoring with component-level inspection and maintenance. Specifically, component-level inspection is triggered when the continuously monitored system performance drops to an inspection threshold, and subsequently, maintenance is conducted for components whose conditions fall below a maintenance threshold. We analytically model the system’s performance degradation and derive its stationary distribution and long-term profit rate under the bi-level policy. The optimal policy is obtained using surrogate optimization to overcome computational complexity. Numerical results demonstrate the impact and effectiveness of the bi-level policy.

title: Probability density integral equation of stochastic dynamic system and time-variant correlation analysis of responses
Random collaborative warranty pricing and out-of-warranty maintenance design for mission-epoch systems
