Seismic-risk-based differentiated reinforcement analysis for ultra-high-voltage converter stations
Post-disaster scheduling of satellite communication vehicles for activating loads
Integrating Social Equity into Resilience-based Post-disaster Recovery of Interdependent Infrastructure Systems
A Bayesian value-of-information framework for inspection planning of marine concrete structures under epistemic uncertainty
Resilience analysis of road transportation-electric power system considering interdependencies under earthquake effects
Resilience assessment method for subsea trees based on probabilistic interval models
Resilience measurement in socio-technical systems: A systematic review
abstract: This study systematically reviews resilience measurement methods in socio-technical systems. Although resilience has become widely measured, current assessment approaches are fragmented and lack conceptual clarity. This study analyzed 192 peer-reviewed studies, and organized their methods into quantitative and qualitative classifications to identify the evolutionary trajectory of methodologies, frequent data collection methods, and relevant domains, and evaluate the measurement tools using 13 methodological criteria and their use of three core resilience components (capacities, abilities, and properties/attributes). Surveys and interviews were the dominant data collection methods for quantitative and qualitative approaches, while most studies used mixed techniques to collect data, and healthcare, maritime, and process industries were the most frequent domains for resilience assessments. The evaluation revealed top-ranking assessment tools, including Bayesian Networks (BN), Functional Resonance Analysis Method (FRAM), Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBN), Machine Learning Algorithms (MLAs), some Index-Based tools, Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS), and Resilience Analysis Grid (RAG). To address conceptual ambiguity and enhance measurement accuracy, this paper proposed a three-layer structured illustration of resilience components and their relationships. It appears that to address the complexity of resilience, integrating hybrid methods with mapping techniques and the proposed three-layer conceptual representation can link resilience levels with emergence, enabling robust, evidence-based assessments in socio-technical systems.

title: HERO: A hybrid expert-relational ontology framework for robust decision-making in the risk management of socio-technical systems
An adaptive and efficient approach for non-Gaussian random buffeting analysis of long-span bridges using direct probability integral method
A comprehensive review of seismic resilience of communication systems: An earthquake engineering perspective
Resilience analysis of multi-modal public transport networks under rainstorm waterlogging disasters: A case study in Chengdu, China
abstract: • A resilience analysis model is proposed for MPT networks under waterlogging. • Waterlogging negative impact and its dynamic propagation process are considered. • The resilience of the bus-rail MPT network in Chengdu is analyzed. Rainstorm waterlogging disasters (RWDs) can severely disrupt the operation of multimodal public transport networks, highlighting the practical significance of assessing their resilience under RWDs. This study develops a resilience analysis model that incorporates the dynamic propagation (DP) of RWD-induced disruptions within a multi-modal public transport (MPT) network. The formulated model is validated through comprehensive numerical experiments on Chengdu’s MPT network consisting of bus and rail services. Results show that the resilience metric is relevant to the total rainfall and its temporal distribution. Meanwhile, the negative effects arising from the DP process must be considered in the network resilience analysis. Sensitivity analysis indicates that urban road drainage capacity is the dominant factor influencing the network resilience. Finally, several practical implications are proposed to enhance the MPT network resilience under RWDs.

title: A modeling framework for the inoperability Assessment of interdependent critical infrastructures exposed to spatially distributed natural hazards
abstract: In this paper, a Dynamic Inoperability Input-Output Model (DIIM) is integrated with a copula-based hazard spatial model to assess the risk of inoperability of critical infrastructures exposed to spatially distributed natural hazards. Copulas are used because they can describe the natural hazard extent across a spatial domain. In particular, Canonical-vine copulas (C-vine) are here used to model the complex spatial dependencies while accounting also for the tail effects typical of extreme hazard events. The proposed modeling framework is applied to a system of systems comprising artifact gas and power networks exposed to extreme wind from Northeast of Italy meteo.

title: Improving resilience of mobile Internet of Things against malware attacks via optimal patch allocation
Maritime accident severity modeling with operationally realistic multi-factor data-driven bayesian networks
abstract: • Trains and benchmarks TAN, ANB, and expert BNs for severity forecasting • Integrates two-layer geography: named sea regions plus operating locale • Uses multi-state met ocean factors: visibility, wind, sea state, storms, ice • Adds PSC inspection outcomes as a compliance signal in severity modelling • Provides scenario, sensitivity, SoI, and TRI analyses for actionable levers Maritime accident severity analysis supports safety management and emergency preparedness, yet operational realism remains limited in many quantitative models. Common limitations include coarse geographic representation, reduced-granularity met-ocean descriptors, and the omission of Port State Control (PSC) compliance signals. These constraints can mask actionable thresholds and hinder the identification of interpretable, decision-relevant severity pathways. To address this, the study develops Bayesian Network (BN) models to forecast accident severity using a globally distributed, multi-year (2015-2024) dataset of 1050 reports, with granular descriptors of route/region, operating locale, weather, sea-state, visibility, ship profile, human error, and accident type. It assembles a harmonized severity dataset unifying investigation narratives, PSC outcomes, ship registries, and met-ocean validation within a single standardized schema; embeds two-layer geography, multi-state environmental conditions, and compliance signals into one BN severity framework; and benchmarks three BN families, Tree-Augmented Naïve (TAN), Augmented Naïve Bayes (ANB), and a literature/expert topology, on the same dataset. Beyond structure comparison, a unified inference workflow combines Strength-of-Influence, state-wise tornado decomposition, True Risk Influence (TRI), and sequential and simultaneous scenario analysis. All three models were estimated via Expectation–Maximization (EM) and evaluated using stratified 10-fold ROC/AUC. The literature/expert BN achieved the strongest cross-validated discrimination across severity states and was selected for analysis, indicating that structure should be selected empirically rather than assumed a priori. Diagnostic, scenario, and sensitivity analysis show that severity escalates when open-sea operations on dense traffic corridors coincide with adverse environment (storm, poor visibility, rough sea, high winds), human error, and loss-of-control typologies (grounding/capsizing); severity attenuates under benign conditions and contact-type events. Strength-of-Influence results highlight the central roles of route/region→traffic density and weather/visibility→severity pathways. A targeted TRI assessment isolates Accident Type as the dominant lever shifting probability mass into the high-severity state. The findings enable consequence-aware routing and vessel traffic prioritization, type-conditioned emergency preparedness, and human-factor/equipment readiness.

title: Risk-stratified facility location framework for heterogeneous unmanned aerial vehicle swarms in drowning rescue: Optimization and socioeconomic evaluation
Cascading failures in interdependent hypergraphs: The role of infection propagation
A novel community-aware random walk for identifying critical nodes in complex networks
Grassroots perceptions-oriented failure mode and effects analysis-II approach with non-cooperative behaviors consideration for new energy security risk assessment
A goal-based, dual-objective approach for designing optimal multi-level accelerated test plans
An adaptive weighted lasso regression method for sparse polynomial chaos expansion: Application to multi-source uncertainty quantification
Real-time crash risk level prediction of freeways based on a hybrid spatiotemporal deep learning framework with channel redistribution
abstract: The accurate prediction of crash risk from massive traffic data has become a critical challenge for enhancing road safety. To improve real-time crash risk prediction capabilities, a novel hybrid deep learning framework combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Transformers, and STar Aggregate-Redistribute (STAR) Module is proposed (i.e., CNN-Transformer-STAR). Using high-resolution vehicle trajectory data from the NGSIM dataset, the model extracts complex spatiotemporal interaction features to classify the crash risks into three categories: low level, medium level, and high level. Specifically, the CNN branch is employed to capture local spatiotemporal dynamics and cross-feature coupling relationships, while the Transformer models global temporal and spatial dependencies. Additionally, the STAR module implements a centralized scheme to extract a global latent representation, which is then redistributed across feature channels to optimize inter-channel interactions. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a superior AUC of 0.90, outperforming baselines. The transferability of the predictive framework is validated using an external dataset, which shows a good robustness (AUC = 0.86) in different freeway scenarios. The results provide policy guidance for freeway traffic safety management.

title: Dynamic branch expansion: A hypergraph-augmented adaptive continual learning framework for machine health prognosis under time-varying conditions
abstract: Industrial data streams with dynamic distributions pose more daunting challenges for data-driven machine health monitoring. Continual learning (CL) method has the ability to adapt to newly-collected data and retain partial memory of previous degradation knowledge, while it still sinks into a dilemma of insufficient accumulation for long-term and diverse degradation patterns under complex operating conditions (OCs). This study proposes an adaptive continuous health prognosis framework with dynamic branch expansion (DBE) for absorbing dynamic data streams to predict the remaining useful life of rotating machines under time-varying OCs. Among it, an OC-aware hypergraph topology network is designed to enhance the hypergraph representation, after which hypergraph topology-memorized knowledge buffer is established for optimal replay sampling. On this basis, an adaptive DBE framework is constructed, which self-recognizes the addition of branches with the continuous influx of new data; and it ingeniously integrates multi-branch predictions via branch discriminator logits at inference stage to enhance CL generalization capability. Case studies of multi-stage continuous prognosis are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results indicate that it can gradually enhance the prediction performance with incremental data, and maintain the predictions of old data while fully learning degraded knowledge at new stages.

title: Markov regenerative process-based framework for reliability and energy efficiency evaluation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle swarm system
Dynamic risk-informed path planning for fire evacuation: An incremental reliability assessment approach
Assessing port resilience to climate change in Asia: A comparative analysis
From Safety-I to Safety-II: longitudinal control strategies for autonomous vehicles based on risk homeostasis theory
Hierarchical domain-physical topology enhanced Fully-Connected Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network for remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Accurate and reliable Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is paramount for ensuring the operational reliability and safety of complex industrial systems. However, existing deep learning paradigms often fail to incorporate explicit structural biases derived from physical dependencies, neglecting inherent physical mechanisms and failing to provide rigorous uncertainty quantification. To surmount these challenges, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Domain-Physical Topology Enhanced Fully-Connected Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network (HDPT-FC-STGNN). First, to bridge the heterogeneity between symbolic domain knowledge and continuous sensor streams, a Hierarchical Domain-Physical Topology (HDPT) is constructed leveraging high-dimensional semantic embeddings. A hierarchical message-passing mechanism is subsequently devised to explicitly encode topological dependencies, thereby fusing static physical priors with dynamic sensor streams. Second, to mitigate spurious correlations in noise-intensive environments, a Structure-Aware Probabilistic Graph Sampling strategy is introduced. By selectively injecting stochasticity into unreliable data-driven edges, this mechanism treats the graph topology as a latent variable, bolstering the model robustness against epistemic ambiguity. Finally, a Bayesian uncertainty quantification module, governed by a risk-sensitive hybrid loss function, is implemented to yield high-fidelity RUL estimates alongside well-calibrated confidence intervals. Extensive experiments on the C-MAPSS benchmark demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both deterministic precision and probabilistic reliability, notably reducing the RMSE by approximately 6.9% on the FD001 subset while ensuring high probabilistic reliability.

title: Assessing redundancy and resilience of roadway networks prone to geohazards in mountainous regions
Knowledge graph-enhanced large language models for explainable causal analysis of crane accidents
abstract: Crane accidents are characterized by high suddenness, chain-like evolution, and strongly coupled causal factors. Traditional experience-driven approaches are insufficient for reliable causal analysis and evidence-grounded interpretation. This study proposes a knowledge graph-enhanced large language model framework for explainable causal analysis and question answering in crane accident scenarios. A domain-specific ontology for crane accident causation is established based on the human-machine-environment-management (HMEM) framework, and a multi-stage automated knowledge extraction pipeline is developed. Using few-shot prompting, relation enrichment, and self-discrimination filtering, the method achieves high-consistency extraction of accident entities and relationships, resulting in a high-quality crane accident knowledge graph. A Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) mechanism is further introduced to integrate BAAI General Embedding (BGE)-based semantic vector retrieval with multi-hop causal path expansion, enabling the retrieval of structurally constrained causal evidence. An evidence-constrained generation strategy ensures that the produced responses are logically coherent, consistent with retrieved causal evidence, and traceable. The CraneSafe QA prototype system supports knowledge extraction, graph visualization, causal chain analysis, and interactive reasoning. Experiments demonstrate improvements in retrieval accuracy, evidence consistency, and noise robustness, with stable performance across queries of varying semantic depth. The results indicate that knowledge graph-enhanced large language models substantially improve the reliability and interpretability of causal analysis in crane accident scenarios.

title: Pump fault diagnosis for vanadium redox flow batteries using an optimized smoothing-based graph convolutional network
abstract: Vanadium redox flow batteries (VRBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage, yet reliable pump fault diagnosis remains challenging due to complex multivariate coupling and limited labeled data. Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) provide an effective way to model variable relationships, but their performance is fundamentally limited by the oversmoothing problem, which leads to loss of feature discriminability in deep architectures. To address this issue, an optimized smoothing-based GCN (OS-GCN) framework is proposed. A smoothing factor (SF) is introduced to regulate feature propagation, and particle swarm optimization is employed to determine its optimal value, enabling a balance between information aggregation and feature preservation. Data association graphs for the GCN are constructed based on Euclidean distance (ED) relationships to capture system dynamics. Pump fault data are collected under both controlled and real-world conditions, providing the basis for an in-depth analysis of operating temperature effects, robustness to noise, and the applicability of the proposed model. Experimental results show that OS-GCN significantly outperforms existing fault diagnosis methods under controlled and real-world conditions. These findings confirm that the proposed framework effectively mitigates oversmoothing and improves the accuracy and robustness of VRB pump fault diagnosis.

title: Reliability-oriented data-physics fusion-driven probabilistic fatigue life prediction of gears and equivalent tooth life conversion
Reliability and maintainability analysis of unmanned aerial vehicle under varied environmental conditions
Bayesian spatio-temporal modeling of Arctic maritime incidents with integrated nested Laplace approximation
Human reliability design method for human-machine interface based on an optimized back propagation neural network under visual cognitive interference
abstract: In the operation of medical equipment, laboratory personnel often fall into visual blurring when facing highly pathogenic dangerous viruses due to wearing goggles for a long time. Under such circumstances, human reliability level is subject to mixed uncertainties due to factors such as human cognition disturbed and so on. Moreover, there is a lack of relevant research. Constructing an appropriate human reliability design method model for Human-Machine Interface (HMI) is crucial for enhancing cognitive interaction level. Firstly, this research adopted the Human Error Assessment and Reduction Technique (HEART) combined with Grey Relational Algorithm (GRA) to measure Human Error Probability (HEP), which can solve that problem about the universality of its quantitative values leading to the uncertainty of matching in actual scenario. By comparing with two similar algorithms, to reduce the uncertainty of high-dimensional data modeling, Levenberg-Marquardt Backpropagation Neural Network (LM-BPNN) optimized by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) was finally selected to construct the design model, fitting the correlation between the operation state and interface elements. Meanwhile, HEP analyzed by improved HEART was taken as one of input features of BPNN. Ultimately, statistical experiment verification shows that this method is effective and can promote the reliable development of medical laboratory systems.

title: CSIR-Net: a continuous spatio-temporal information redundancy network based on structural priors for satellite telemetry data reliability enhancement
abstract: Enhancing satellite telemetry reliability is essential for status assessment and operational management. However, telemetry data have complex spatio-temporal dependencies and diverse missing patterns, making it challenging for traditional methods with discrete modeling, fixed parameters, and static prediction steps to recover. To address these, this paper proposes a continuous spatio-temporal information redundancy network that transforms degraded discrete data recovery into timestamp-aware continuous-trajectory inference with uncertainty-calibrated selection. Specifically, a long short-term memory network is reconstructed using neural stochastic differential equations to model hidden-state evolution in continuous time, and Ito integrals are incorporated to characterize uneven observation gaps, thereby enabling recovery at arbitrary timestamps. Additionally, time-varying signals and Brownian perturbations are integrated into the model to allow dynamic adjustment of parameters with the input, thereby improving the ability to recover multiple evolving features. Finally, a structure-prior-guided hierarchical graph is constructed to fuse multi-scale dependencies while suppressing redundant error propagation, and multi-head graph attention is used to derive adaptive confidence intervals for selective recovery, thereby improving telemetry reliability without obscuring novel patterns. Experiments on five datasets show the proposed method improves recovery accuracy by 27.7% over the best baseline, achieves 15.2–78.5 ms batch latency, and has strong potential for real-time large-scale telemetry reliability.

title: Automated design for safety performance evaluation system using accident probability and risk cost analytics: A case study of industrial construction
A coupled dynamic model for pedestrian evacuation and risk assessment during toxic gas leakage in underground spaces
Risk-oriented degradation modeling and maintenance decision support for computed tomography X-ray tubes using mechanism-informed learning
abstract: Accurate estimation of the remaining useful life (RUL) of Computed Tomography (CT) X-ray tubes is essential for maintaining medical service continuity, reducing failure risk, and minimizing unplanned downtime. However, intrinsic degradation patterns are often obscured by heterogeneous operating conditions, such as automatic tube current modulation and voltage optimization. To address this challenge, we propose the Hybrid Affine Gated Fusion Network (HAGF-Net), a deep learning framework tailored for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments. HAGF-Net employs a dual-branch parallel architecture that integrates physical priors with data-driven features. One branch processes Mechanism-driven Indicators (MDIs) derived from filament degradation physics, including cathode degradation rate (CDR) and degradation kinetic increment (DKI), using a Conditioned Operating-Gated Transformer (COG-Transformer) that dynamically modulates attention weights based on discrete operational states. Simultaneously, a raw-signal Branch based on CNN-LSTM modules captures local fluctuations and long-term temporal dependencies from multi-dimensional sensor sequences. The framework was validated on a high-resolution IoMT dataset comprising 10 Philips X-ray tubes from multiple clinical sites across China (2017–2024), covering their entire service lives. HAGF-Net demonstrates high global predictive accuracy (RMSE = 0.07) and precise final-stage performance (MAE ≈ 3.85 days) and 95% prediction intervals close to the nominal coverage across sites. Ablation and comparison studies indicate that incorporating physical MDIs and condition-aware gating mechanisms enhances model’s robustness and responsiveness to complex degradation dynamics. Under simulated unreliable monitoring conditions, the proposed method evaluates model robustness under reduced sampling frequencies, demonstrating stable performance across different levels of data sparsity.

title: Enhancing lifecycle resilience of urban road networks under uncertainty: A two-stage stochastic programming approach for integrated reinforcement and restoration
An explicit surrogate model for real-time reliability assessment of face stability in underwater slurry shield tunneling
abstract: Ensuring tunnel face stability in underwater slurry shield tunneling is challenging due to the inherent stochasticity of geotechnical parameters. Despite their advantages, current frameworks face practical limitations: RFM rigorously captures spatial variability, but its computational cost hinders real-time deployment. Conversely, machine learning based RVMs rely on opaque models lacking explicit expressions, restricting their engineering portability. Importantly, groundwater effects are frequently not properly incorporated into existing frameworks. This study proposes a transparent, efficient reliability assessment framework that incorporates groundwater via the effective stress principle and the upper-bound theorem of limit analysis. A high-fidelity dataset of 4000 samples, accounting for parameter cross-correlations, is used to train a Back-Propagation Neural Network (BPNN). By extracting an explicit algebraic expression from the network, the framework eliminates model opacity and platform dependency. Combined with Sobol sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulations, this surrogate model facilitates real-time determination of reliability-based face support pressure. Results indicate that the reliability-based surrogate model achieves an instantaneous execution time of 0.3 s, marking a substantial acceleration from the 55 h required by the traditional RFM. Moreover, it yields more conservative design values, thereby providing an additional safety buffer for engineering applications. Field validation at the Jiangyin-Jingjiang Yangtze River Tunnel confirms the framework's practical utility for real-time safety assessment in sandy strata.

title: Sustainable engineering decisions toward nature-based solutions for flood protection infrastructure: An integrated system dynamics framework
abstract: Flood protection infrastructure is increasingly challenged by aging systems, climate impacts, and public expectations for environmentally conscious design. Although innovative approaches such as nature-based solutions (NBS) can enhance long-term reliability, ecosystem health, and community resilience, their adoption remains limited. Engineering decisions are still dominated by technical and regulatory constraints, with limited attention to behavioral and organizational factors. This study addresses this gap by developing an integrated system dynamics model (SDM) grounded in the Value-Belief-Norm (VBN) framework, Bass innovation diffusion, and information cascade theories. Using a mixed-methods approach, interviews and surveys with U.S. engineers, key behavioral drivers were identified. These insights were translated into feedback structures to simulate long-term changes in engineering norms and decisions as drivers to infrastructure reliability. Scenario analyses reveal that stronger community engagement, supportive policies, and enhanced collaboration accelerate NBS adoption and reduce resistance over time. Conversely, weak institutional support and conservative norms hinder transitions and reinforce eco-skeptical attitudes. The SDM-driven framework provides a dynamic lens through which cognitive and organizational factors in sustainable infrastructure transitions can be examined together, offering a foundation for evidence-based policy design, professional training, and data-driven model calibration.

title: Editorial Board
Incremental dynamic analysis via hierarchical Bayesian modelling for efficient seismic fragility analysis and uncertainty quantification
abstract: • Hierarchical Bayesian model (HBM) captures inter- and intra-ground motion variability in Incremental Dynamic Analysis (IDA). • Updated HBM robustly estimates full nonlinear time-history analysis (NLTHA) outputs even with limited NLTHAs. • HB-IDA limits errors in final seismic fragility curves to within 4% while requiring only about 26% of the computational cost of conventional IDA in the example. • By combining measured NLTHA results with Bayesian-predicted responses, HB-IDA generates fragility curves with credible uncertainty bands, yielding more realistic seismic performance estimates than conventional IDA. • A highly efficient intensity measure does not necessarily yield more reliable fragility estimates, as it may underestimate uncertainty in unobserved cases. Broadening the variety of NLTHA evidence yields greater improvements in uncertainty quantification than merely increasing the number of simulations. Seismic fragility analysis of structures is crucial for performance-based earthquake engineering. Incremental Dynamic Analysis (IDA) demands extensive nonlinear time‐history analyses (NLTHA) across multiple ground motion (GM) records and intensity levels, making it time‐consuming. To mitigate costs and quantify uncertainty in IDA, this study introduces a Hierarchical Bayesian IDA framework (HB-IDA). HB-IDA treats each ground motion as a basic unit and uses a two-level Bayesian model to capture both inter- and intra-GM variability. Exploiting similarity among GMs, HB-IDA fully scales only a small subset of motions (those with the shortest duration). The remaining motions undergo a single NLTHA run, and their missing responses are predicted by the Bayesian model. By combining NLTHA outputs with Bayesian predictions, HB-IDA produces fragility curves with clear uncertainty bands that better reflect realistic structural behavior, achieving a balance between accuracy and robustness. Moreover, the optimal intensity measure that fits the model best may not necessarily improve realism, and that widening the range of evidence yields greater benefits than simply running more NLTHA cases. Using underground tunnels within a representative liquefiable soil profile as case studies, this study highlights the potential of integrating surrogate models and hierarchical Bayes to provide efficient and robust fragility analysis.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-driven resilience optimization for infrastructure systems: A socio-technical perspective integrating functional resonance analysis method
abstract: Escalating natural disasters and growing infrastructure complexity render resilience optimization indispensable for sustaining operations and mitigating losses. While deep reinforcement learning (DRL) offers powerful optimization potential, current models often overlook the interactions and variability inherent in socio-technical systems. Integrating DRL with the functional resonance analysis method (FRAM) shows promise, yet remains impractical without a dedicated focus on resilience-oriented controls. Accordingly, this paper proposes a FRAM-DRL framework tailored for infrastructure resilience optimization. Its key advancements are threefold: (1) extending FRAM into a multi-stage structure to capture socio-technical features throughout the resilience lifecycle; (2) establishing variability analysis rules to transform qualitative FRAM into an interactive environment; and (3) defining FRAM-based state, action, and reward representations to facilitate DRL training. The framework was applied to urban metro system (UMS) resilience under extreme rainfall, leveraging the Nanjing Metro case. Results demonstrate that the Dueling DQN performed best among the tested value-based architectures, with action constraint (κ=4) providing the optimal balance between optimization gain and cost efficiency. The learned policies prioritize high-leverage domains and early-stage controls, achieving a favorable reward-efficiency advantage over heuristic strategies via global policy search. Overall, this work methodologically advances Safety-II-oriented proactive management, offering a transferable basis for broader resilience research.

title: Editorial Board
AL-IDNN: Active learning method based on incremental updating of deep neural networks for structural reliability analysis
abstract: Reliability analysis is essential for ensuring the safety of engineering systems under uncertainty. In reliability analysis, surrogate models are widely used to reduce computational cost. However, improving the accuracy of reliability analysis typically requires the continuous introduction of critical samples and repeated reconstruction of the surrogate model. To improve model accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency, this paper proposes an active learning method for structural reliability analysis based on incremental updating of deep neural networks (AL-IDNN). The proposed method preserves the knowledge learned by the existing model through parameter inheritance, thereby eliminating the need to retrain the model from scratch. Meanwhile, an adaptive sampling strategy is employed to enrich the design of experiments (DOEs). By combining model predictions with the distribution characteristics of the sample space, critical samples near the limit state surface (LSS) are identified. Furthermore, the DOEs updating strategy is introduced to control sample quality and improve the fitting accuracy to the LSS. Comparative studies with similar methods are conducted to evaluate the proposed AL-IDNN method. Results from benchmark examples and a prestressed hollow slab girder bridge case demonstrate its effectiveness in terms of both accuracy and efficiency in reliability analysis.

title: A gas turbine performance mitigation control method based on state assessment
Evolving toward robustness: A dynamic weighted multi-layer supply chain network framework with heterogeneous and adaptive mechanisms
Dynamic data processing, backup and abort strategy for cloud computing systems
Time-variant reliability of natural gas pipelines considering trivariate spatial correlation of corrosion defects using limited in-line inspection data
A novel deep joint distribution alignment network for unsupervised remaining useful life prediction via variational auto-encoder
Quantifying reliability-relevant delay variability in remote-stand ground handling: Evidence from a multi-airport matched comparison
A Shapley-value cooperative game-based risk decision model for natural gas pipeline vulnerability
Research on human reliability analysis method for digital main control room of nuclear power plants based on Bayesian network
Decision reliability analysis framework for intelligent unmanned system-of-systems using the cooperative multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient
abstract: The decision reliability is the capability of the intelligent unmanned system-of-systems (IUSoS) to make and execute decisions under a disturbed environment. However, the inherent uncertainty of individual autonomy may render decisions unreliable, leading to task failures and resource wastage. To address this issue, we propose a novel decision reliability analysis framework for the IUSoS using the cooperative multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (C-MADDPG). Firstly, considering individual autonomy and functional diversity, a multilayer operation network based on graph coloring theory is established to provide a foundation for decision analysis. Secondly, a distributed decision model based on the enhanced actor-critic (AC) architecture is presented to maintain the individual stable decision-making ability. Thirdly, considering the impact of individual decisions on reliability, an operation-loop-oriented decision reliability assessment model is proposed to quantify decision reliability. Then, the decision reliability is optimized by the C-MADDPG algorithm, which updates the enhanced AC network with the cooperative reward. Finally, a case study on a multi-agent collaborative scenario demonstrates the feasibility of the methodology. The proposed method receives the most rewards compared with variant algorithms and consistently outperforms them in task completion degree, providing a technical approach for improving system-of-systems reliability under distributed architectures and demonstrating that the cooperative reward mechanism balances individual autonomy with system reliability.

title: Toward future flight safety of electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft: Applying black swan to safety risk assessment of emerging technologies
Exploring the dynamic robustness of metro-bus composite networks considering passenger spatiotemporal heterogeneity and behavior characteristics
Physics-informed neural networks for Fokker–Planck–Kolmogorov equations corresponding to systems with tempered stable Lévy noise
abstract: Tempered stable Lévy noise has a greater advantage in fitting real systems due to its finite variance, compared with α-stable Lévy noise. The responses of a system under tempered stable Lévy noise are governed by a tempered fractional Fokker–Planck-Kolmogorov (FPK) equation, which is difficult to solve due to the nonlocal property of the tempered fractional derivative. In this paper, we propose the tempered fractional physics-informed neural networks (TF-PINNs) for solving the FPK equations corresponding to systems driven by tempered stable Lévy noise. Firstly, we derive the corresponding tempered fractional FPK equation by means of characteristic function, Chapman–Kolmogorov-Smoluchowski equation, and Fourier transformation. Secondly, we extend the PINNs to solve the tempered fractional FPK equation by incorporating discretized tempered fractional derivatives into the loss function of the neural network. In particular, in addition to solving the system response, the proposed TF-PINNs framework can also identify the unknown parameters in the system. Finally, three typical examples are implemented to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the presented algorithm compared with finite difference solutions and Monte Carlo simulations.

title: Economically driven multi-dimensional strategies for enhancing substation seismic resilience: Integrating machine learning and heuristic optimization algorithms
abstract: Developing seismic resilience enhancement strategies for substations requires not only improving system functionality but also integrating economic analysis to support investment decisions. This study proposes an economic-driven framework for substation seismic resilience enhancement. Spare parts inventory and equipment mobilization mechanisms are incorporated to extend a shortest-path-based repair strategy, capturing post-earthquake recovery under complex operating conditions. Typical scenarios are constructed and large sample sets are generated to train machine learning models, which serve as surrogate models for rapid resilience assessment and iterative strategy optimization. A global economic evaluation model integrates resource inputs and post-earthquake returns to quantify the cost–benefit characteristics of different strategies. Heuristic algorithms are used to optimize strategy variables and systematically analyze the evolution of economic benefits and investment preferences under complex scenarios involving varying earthquake intensities and resource constraints. The framework is demonstrated on a 220 kV substation system, and the results confirm the substantial return on investment of seismic resilience enhancement strategies. Furthermore, equipment reinforcement is shown to provide greater economic benefits than spare parts inventory, highlighting the importance of rational cost allocation. Overall, the proposed framework enables quantitative cost–benefit analysis and supports practical investment decision-making in seismic resilience enhancement.

title: Maintenance optimization in multi-component production systems: A stochastic degradation-aware evolutionary reinforcement learning framework
abstract: Complex manufacturing systems, characterized by interdependent components and stochastic disruptions, present critical challenges in optimizing maintenance planning under uncertainty. To address this gap, we propose the Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning (ES-ERL) framework, which integrates evolutionary reinforcement learning with ordinary differential equation-based system dynamics to derive adaptive maintenance policies. The ES-ERL algorithm dynamically optimizes policy exploration by coupling real-time degradation patterns with system-level interdependencies, ensuring robustness against stochastic component interactions. Experimental validation using industrially-representative scenarios demonstrates the framework’s superiority over state-of-the-art benchmarks, including genetic algorithm and artificial immune system-based methods. Specifically, ES-ERL achieves 15% faster convergence and improves final solution quality by 12% compared to existing approaches. Furthermore, the framework systematically balances reliability and cost efficiency while scaling to high-dimensional component networks, offering a principled approach for resilient industrial cyber–physical systems.

title: Cascading failure analysis of critical infrastructure in conflict zones: a large language model-driven knowledge graph framework
abstract: Modern geopolitical conflicts increasingly target interdependent critical infrastructures, where localized damage can trigger cascading failures, leading to widespread disruption of essential public services. Traditional intelligence safety assessment frameworks struggle to process the dynamic, unstructured data streams from conflict environments. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a novel probabilistic framework for dynamic cascading failure analysis of Critical Infrastructure (CI) under attacks by integrating Large Language Model (LLM) and Knowledge Graph (KG). Our novel dual-graph architecture first employs an LLM to automatically construct a Dynamic Battlefield Event Knowledge Graph (BEKG) from real-time Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT), capturing tactical events as they unfold. This dynamic event layer then serves as evidence for a probabilistic inference process on a static Infrastructure Service Dependency Knowledge Graph (ISDKG), which is modeled as a Bayesian Network (BN). This integration enables the simulation of the propagation of cascading failures, translating initial physical damage into a quantifiable risk assessment of widespread service disruptions. Validated through a case study on Ukraine's infrastructure, our system demonstrates high fidelity in automated knowledge construction, provides novel insights into cascading impact analysis, and offers a powerful decision-support tool for assessing the systemic vulnerability and resilience of complex infrastructure networks in conflict zones.

title: Quantifying the effects of time pressure on pilot situation awareness error in aviation emergencies
Mitigation action-dependent prediction of nuclear plant parameters for severe accident management via conditional generative model
abstract: Effective severe accident management in nuclear power plants requires situational awareness to anticipate multivariate plant responses under time pressure and uncertainty. While artificial intelligence–based surrogate models can support real-time decisions, many studies use recursive multistep forecasting, which tends to accumulate errors over long horizons and often does not reflect operator mitigation actions explicitly. This study proposes an action-conditioned, multivariate multistep prediction model for severe accident decision support. By integrating a transformer, Autoformer, temporal convolutional network, and conditional variational autoencoder, the model produces direct multi-horizon forecasts with uncertainty estimates and represents mitigation actuation states as conditional inputs. For model training and testing, a database was generated using the MAAP 5.06 code with optimized discretization intervals used for data generation and Latin hypercube sampling applied to obtain representative severe accident scenarios with reduced computational cost. The resulting action-conditioned predictions support technical support center staff and plant operators in comparing mitigation options against a no-action baseline and also in assessing key safety-related trends during severe accident progression.

title: A proactive safety management method in machining workshops driven by expert knowledge and hybrid retrieval-augmented generation
A resilient unmanned swarm model considering visual occlusion and dynamic time warping
Dynamic reliability analysis for unmanned systems with epistemic uncertainty: An application to the variable buoyancy system of a self-powered underwater glider
Single sensor mechanical construction health monitoring using cross-entropy of frequency spectra
abstract: A robust and periodic damage-detection strategy is needed for structures that operate under stochastic ambient excitation and cannot be instrumented densely or inspected frequently. This paper proposes a response-only, single-sensor method for monitoring global structural change from low-signal-to-noise vibration data. The method forms a multiscale spectral footprint of the undamaged state and compares subsequent measurements by softmax normalization and cumulative cross-entropy, yielding a damage-severity indicator. The approach is validated on long-term field measurements of light poles subjected to accelerated ageing. To position the method against conventional operational modal analysis (OMA), OMA-based natural frequency tracking was also evaluated on the same data set. In the present measurements, the relation between period-wise natural frequency shift and the known damage chronology was weak and non-uniform across poles, indicating that direct frequency tracking alone did not provide a sufficiently reliable standalone deterioration indicator. By contrast, the proposed cross-entropy-based comparison distinguished damaged poles from the intact reference despite indistinct modal shifts, unknown excitation, and low-quality single-sensor data. The results support the method as a practical low-cost early-warning tool for global structural change detection in long-term monitoring applications where conventional modal indicators are difficult to extract robustly from field data.

title: Quantifying interface–procedure coupling risks in digital nuclear control rooms: An event-based human reliability assessment
Correlated failure and repair times in reliability: A bivariate exponential model
Probabilistic deep learning regression framework for post-hazard hurricane wind damage assessment of buildings
abstract: Hurricanes significantly affect coastal communities, causing substantial disruption to their socio-economic systems. Therefore, post-hurricane rapid assessment is essential for effective disaster response and recovery. Traditional human-based assessments through field reconnaissance are time-consuming, leading to delays in critical decision-making. Therefore, machine learning and deep learning have emerged as powerful alternatives enabling automated, near-real-time damage evaluation. By leveraging data from past expert-classified and systematically organized events, new models can predict damage either immediately after or even during a hurricane event. This study introduces a probabilistic deep learning regression framework that predicts component-level building damage percentages using multi-view geo-coded post-disaster imagery. Unlike conventional classification models, the proposed approach estimates continuous damage ratios for eight key envelope components, enabling more detailed and loss-relevant characterization of structural damage. A pretrained convolutional backbone is integrated with a regression head to fuse features extracted from multiple building views, while a systematic hyperparameter sensitivity analysis is performed to optimize model performance. To enhance the reliability of the developed model, uncertainty quantification was incorporated using Monte Carlo dropout and bootstrapping techniques, producing confidence intervals for each prediction. Post-disaster images from Hurricane Harvey (2017), covering 436 buildings, were used as a case study to build this model. Results demonstrate that the distribution of training data strongly influences prediction accuracy across components. Both uncertainty quantification methods performed well in capturing mean values, though they diverged in their confidence intervals. Bootstrapping offered superior uncertainty characterization, albeit with a higher computational cost compared to the Monte Carlo approach.

title: Safe Cross-Entropy importance sampling for extremely small failure probabilities
An improved GO-FLOW model for reliability analysis and prediction of cold-standby systems
Dual-modality vessel trajectory anomaly detection for maritime risk prevention based on automatic identification system data
Robust reinforcement learning with graph neural networks for stochastic urban rail daily maintenance scheduling
abstract: Urban rail daily maintenance scheduling is challenged by urgent task insertions, limited time windows, and multi-resource requirements. This paper formulates the problem as a stochastic resource-constrained project scheduling problem on dynamic directed acyclic graphs and proposes a preference-conditioned graph neural network (GNN) and deep reinforcement learning framework for real-time rescheduling. The GNN combines precedence-aware propagation and change-decaying message passing to encode topology shifts after interruptions and insertions, while deterministic action masking guarantees precedence- and resource-feasible decisions. The policy is conditioned on a dispatcher-specified preference vector and trained with an Augmented Tchebycheff objective, enabling online adaptation among makespan, overtime penalty, financial cost, maintenance quality, and resource fairness without retraining. Experiments on PSPLIB show near-optimal static performance, including a 0.29% optimality gap on J120 with linear inference complexity. In stochastic insertion environments, the method achieves strong Pareto-front quality in hypervolume, IGD, and non-dominated solutions, while obtaining the best fixed-preference composite cost with sub-second inference latency. It also demonstrates robust cross-scale and zero-shot transfer to the Shenzhen Metro network. On real-world metro data, the framework achieves an average makespan of 625.03 min in 1.17 s, while additional stress tests verify its robustness, interpretability, and industrial applicability.

title: Resilience enhancement of distribution network through dynamic topology reconfiguration and mobile microgrid deployment
Monotonicity-constrained ordinal Gaussian process for seismic fragility modeling
abstract: This study proposes a unified ordinal Gaussian process (GP) framework that places a GP prior on latent functions and integrates three classical ordinal regression models, namely cumulative, sequential, and adjacent-category models, thereby providing a flexible nonparametric alternative to lognormal fragility models. Using the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake bridge damage dataset, eleven models are compared under a standardized training and evaluation protocol. The results show that the category specific sequential GP model, SequentialGP-CS, achieves the best overall predictive performance, reducing the ranked probability score (RPS) by 3.4%, reducing the mean binary score (MBS) by 1.2%, and improving the quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) by 6.4% relative to the ProbitOP baseline, while preventing fragility curve crossings by construction. To mitigate local fluctuations that may arise in nonlinear GP models trained on highly scattered samples, three strategies are examined to encourage monotonic fragility curves: a smoothness prior on the kernel hyperparameters, difference-based regularization of the output probabilities, and derivative-based constraints on latent functions. These strategies substantially reduce monotonicity violations, although they are accompanied by slight decreases in predictive performance; among them, the derivative-based constraint reduces the mean violation rate from 10.00% to 0.00% and yields RPS/MBS/QWK of 0.0884/0.6933/0.5870 under the monotonicity requirement.

title: Intelligent prediction of cylinder head cracking in commercial vehicle natural gas engines using hybrid modeling approaches
System risk assessment under urban flooding disaster based on spatialized cascade network
Probabilistic framework for seismic risk analysis of process plants
Dynamic vulnerability assessment of urban rail transit systems using spatiotemporal deep learning
abstract: A dynamic vulnerability assessment framework that integrates deep learning and complex networks is proposed to better understand the responses of urban rail transit (URT) systems to various disruptions. Specifically, a spatiotemporal deep learning model is developed to forecast network passenger flows over different time periods. A node importance evaluation method considering dynamic travel demands and static network structural characteristics is presented. A comprehensive metric is designed to assess both structural and functional vulnerabilities of the network. The proposed method is validated using Shanghai's URT system as a case study. The results reveal that: (1) The proposed graph convolutional network-temporal kolmogorov-arnold network (GCN-TKAN) model accurately predicts passenger flows across different time periods, achieving an average R² of 0.865 on the testing data, an improvement of 0.056 compared to the second-best model (TKAN); (2) When a sequential single-node attack, guided by the proposed node-importance metric, removes the top 5% of stations, overall network performance drops by 45.00%, which is 4.92% higher than the average decline caused by other basic attack strategies. The innovation of this study lies in the joint modeling of time-varying passenger flows and spatial topological properties, which accurately quantifies the network's vulnerability under different disturbance scenarios, providing a theoretical basis for enhancing system resilience.

title: Resilient groundwater flow modeling in heterogeneous porous media using mixed-form physics-informed neural networks and transfer learning
abstract: Reliable modeling of groundwater flow in heterogeneous porous media is crucial for the safety and risk assessment of geotechnical and underground infrastructures, where strong subsurface heterogeneity and frequent scenario updates often constrain the effectiveness of conventional numerical solvers and data-driven surrogates. This study develops a mixed-form physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) framework that simultaneously solves for hydraulic head and Darcy velocity, avoiding second-order derivatives and enhancing numerical stability under strongly heterogeneous permeability fields. Spatial heterogeneity is represented via Karhunen–Loève (KL) expansions with controllable correlation lengths, enabling systematic evaluation across statistically consistent permeability realizations. Benchmark tests involving natural gradients and pumping scenarios demonstrate that the mixed-form PINNs can provide more robust predictions under different heterogeneous permeability distributions. To enhance adaptability, transfer learning is incorporated to reuse trained representations across boundary conditions, pumping configurations, and heterogeneous fields, yielding substantial reductions in retraining cost while preserving prediction quality. The results also reveal that transfer directionality (e.g., from more heterogeneous to less heterogeneous fields) is a key factor affecting generalization efficiency. Rather than replacing conventional solvers, the proposed framework offers a flexible, mesh-free alternative for applications requiring frequent model updates or involving intricate subsurface variability, contributing to more resilient and adaptable groundwater modeling in geotechnical practice.

title: A semi-observable state-driven self-tuning remaining useful life prediction method for mechanical systems
Reliability assessment of aged interdependent power-gas systems under deterioration uncertainty and information loss
Influence regulation in networks and its metaheuristic solution
An adaptive multi-dimensional protection framework for 5G cloud-native networks using collaborative multi-agent systems
abstract: With the deep integration of cloud infrastructure and 5G, microservices have become the mainstream architecture for operators to deliver core network services to 5G users. However, the fine-grained nature of such services also expands the attack surface, introducing new security risks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a dynamic security policy configuration framework for microservices. Based on the Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) algorithm, the framework resolves high-dimensional collaborative decision-making problems in microservice scenarios through cooperative gaming and state sharing among intelligent agents. Compared with existing static or single-agent solutions, our framework enables more efficient security collaboration in multi-agent environments. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the framework can dynamically formulate security protection and quality of service (QoS) assurance strategies according to the current system state, thereby effectively resisting continuous adversarial attacks while minimizing the impact on service quality.

title: An anomalous behavior detection framework for inland vessels using automatic identification system data
Estimating whole-of-event consequences in interdependent infrastructure systems
abstract: Conventional risk assessments underestimate the total burden of hazards by characterizing consequences at or near the point of disruption, rather than as processes that unfold over time. This paper addresses that limitation by introducing a method to estimate whole-of-event consequences in interdependent infrastructure systems, integrating cascading failures and recovery dynamics into time-dependent risk metrics. We develop a modeling framework that generates trajectories of service disruption and restoration across electricity, water, and wastewater networks, and quantify community-level consequences using metrics such as property-days without service, outage duration thresholds, and spatial disparities in recovery. Applied to a coastal flooding case study, the results show that recovery-informed estimates differ substantially from exposure-based and static cascading approaches, revealing both greater total impacts and different spatial distributions of disruption. These findings demonstrate that a substantial portion of risk arises from the accumulation of disruption during recovery, which is not captured in conventional assessments. Whole-of-event consequences therefore provide a more appropriate basis for understanding systemic risk and for informing infrastructure investment, adaptation planning, and risk prioritization. By operationalizing consequence as a time-dependent, system-wide process, this work advances risk assessment practice and supports more accurate and equitable decision-making in interdependent infrastructure systems.

title: Post-earthquake functionality assessment and resilience enhancement of interdependent electric power and mobile communication networks
Multi-mode degradation assessment and vibro-acoustic monitoring of harmonic drive for aerospace applications
Active Bayesian support vector regression with importance sampling for rare event reliability analysis
abstract: Importance sampling achieves variance reduction by introducing an importance sampling density function, and it is one of the most promising methods for reliability analysis. This paper aims to further improve the efficiency and accuracy of importance sampling by integrating the Bayesian support vector regression model with an active learning strategy, thereby enabling its application to a broad spectrum of engineering problems involving rare event analysis. To achieve this, we propose a novel learning function and a new candidate samples construction method that allow the model to actively select training points near the failure surface, characterized by the highest prediction error and greatest spatial diversity. Additionally, we introduce a stopping criterion based on the global prediction error across unclassified points, ensuring that the algorithm terminates with sufficient accuracy. Through both academic case studies and practical engineering examples, we demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional importance sampling methods as well as other active learning surrogate modeling techniques in terms of efficiency and accuracy.

title: Optimization of risk-based and cost-minimized maintenance strategy for corroded pipeline using reinforcement learning
abstract: This study proposes an innovative reinforcement learning (RL)-based approach for long-term maintenance planning in multi-zone pipeline systems. The RL-based model aims to optimize maintenance decisions by minimizing total life-cycle cost. A modified Bayesian Neural Network (BNN) was first developed to predict corrosion depth and length. Failure probabilities before and after repair were then calculated. The Dueling Deep Q-Network (Dueling DQN) model was employed to find an optimal, zone-specific maintenance strategy. A comprehensive sensitivity analysis was also conducted to evaluate the impact of key parameters, including consequence cost, failure probability threshold, composite repair effectiveness and operating pressure. Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the RL model in providing an adaptive and efficient approach to pipeline maintenance under corrosion growth uncertainty. Higher consequence costs and stricter failure probability thresholds lead to earlier interventions, while weaker repair effectiveness causes the model to schedule more frequent maintenance actions. Higher operating pressure significantly increases failure risk and total cost. Under extremely high operating pressure, using replacement at the beginning provides greater long-term benefits than using composite wrap. This study provides a framework for data-driven, risk-based maintenance decision-making in complex pipeline systems.

title: Modeling and reliability assessment method for multi-stress accelerated degradation of motor spindle based on crack time-domain uncertain evolution
Methodological issues and design of solutions for ensuring reliability of heating systems serving large industrial complexes
A dual-network framework for analyzing structural correspondence between train flows and human error patterns across high-speed railway dispatching consoles
Modeling the port-shipping company game under extreme weather event impact: A multi-agent reinforcement learning-based approach
abstract: Extreme weather events (EWEs) significantly disrupt port operations, creating highly uncertain environments that challenge effective recovery planning for both ports and shipping companies. Existing approaches, particularly those based on evolutionary game theory (EGT), typically rely on static payoff structures and myopic decision-making, limiting their ability to capture system dynamics and long-term strategic interactions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework based on the Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) algorithm. The framework models recovery investment decisions by port authorities and cargo transfer strategies by shipping companies as continuous, state-dependent actions that evolve over time in a stochastic recovery process. Comparative experiments against a state-dependent EGT (s-EGT) benchmark demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance in terms of cumulative returns and recovery efficiency. Specifically, the MARL framework learns forward-looking policies that explicitly account for how current decisions influence future system states, even when optimal strategies involve short-term sacrifices. In contrast, the s-EGT model fails to capture these intertemporal effects due to its limited representation of state transitions. The results show that the proposed method accelerates system recovery, improving port efficiency recovery rates by approximately 30% and reducing average vessel waiting times by nearly 80%. Furthermore, cross-scenario fine-tuning experiments indicate that the learned policies generalize well to new disruption scenarios while maintaining stable behavioral patterns. The findings highlight the potential of MARL as an effective decision-support tool for adaptive recovery management in port-shipping systems under extreme weather disruptions.

title: Cross scenarios interpretable quantification of maintenance action effects on system health via liquid Kolmogorov–Arnold operator based framework
abstract: Predictive maintenance for safety–critical assets demands accurate forecasting and interpretable understanding of how maintenance actions affect system health across diverse regimes. We introduce a liquid Kolmogorov–Arnold operator (KAO)-based model that learns a physically grounded health indicator (HI) while revealing maintenance-driven degradation dynamics. The model comprises three components: (i) a BoltzmannKAN attention layer learning per-channel thresholds and temperatures to identify key sensors before and after maintenance; (ii) a self-organizing pool of interpretable operators representing distinct degradation modes, connected via liquid, temperature-controlled soft routing for smooth regime transitions; and (iii) unsupervised contrastive learning around maintenance events anchoring the HI without remaining useful life (RUL) labels, guided by a unified loss combining reconstruction, maintenance-quality classification, and regularization terms. The liquid-KAO framework generates a forward-looking HI reflecting both short-term recovery and long-term degradation moderation, while its autoregressive design enables post-maintenance forecasting and counterfactual analysis. On C-MAPSS with simulated interventions, it provides stable forecasts and identifies mechanism shifts consistent with injected actions; on the real-world National General Aviation Flight Information Database (NGAFID) aircraft maintenance dataset (14 maintenance classes), it achieves 0.84 accuracy, surpassing prior baselines with subsystem-level interpretability and HI-based reliability metrics. Overall, liquid-KAO unifies accuracy, transferability, and equation-level interpretability for reliable maintenance validation and scheduling.

title: A graph neural network-based multi-agent reinforcement learning model for efficient power distribution system recovery after hurricanes
abstract: The rising severity and frequency of hurricanes threaten the resilience of power distribution systems and increase the urgency of improving post-disaster recovery. Beyond capital-intensive grid hardening, fast and cost-effective restoration strategies are essential for reducing outage impacts. Effective recovery requires an optimized sequence of repairs that accounts for network topology, multi-crew coordination, and load prioritization. Traditional optimization and heuristic methods struggle to scale due to the combinatorial repair space and computational burden. To address this challenge, we propose MAGNN–A2C, a graph-based multi-agent actor–critic framework that integrates reinforcement learning, graph neural networks, and centralized training with decentralized execution to learn coordinated, topology-aware repair policies. Reinforcement learning enables reusable repair policies for rapid decision-making, the multi-agent formulation reflects parallel field crews, and graph neural networks encode system interdependencies to support scalable coordination. Evaluation on a real-world-scale case study of Galveston Island, Texas, using public infrastructure and hazard data, shows that MAGNN–A2C consistently outperforms rule-based heuristics and genetic algorithms in restoring load, reducing socioeconomic outage costs, and accelerating recovery trajectories. The learned policy also generalizes to unseen storm tracks and damage patterns, demonstrating robust performance across scenarios. These results highlight a scalable and practically deployable approach for improving distribution system restoration under increasingly severe hurricanes.

title: Flow matching-guided adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo with deep generative proposals for Bayesian model updating in structural health monitoring
abstract: Bayesian model updating (BMU) is essential to probabilistic parameter estimation and system identification in structural health monitoring (SHM). Although Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods are widely regarded as the gold standard for BMU, their high computational cost often limits practical application to large-scale engineering structures. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel BMU framework termed Flow Matching-Guided MCMC (FM-G-MCMC). The framework integrates a multi-chain adaptive MCMC scheme with a deep generative model through an iterative cycle of local sampling, flow training, and global proposal generation. Specifically, local samples generated by gradient-based MCMC kernels are used to train and fine-tune a continuous normalizing flow (CNF) which is learned using flow matching. The trained CNF is then embedded into an independent Metropolis–Hastings kernel to provide efficient global proposals that enable non-local exploration of the parameter space. Accepted samples from both local and global moves are aggregated to adaptively refine the CNF and local proposals in a bidirectional manner, allowing the two components to co-evolve toward the target posterior. Three engineering examples, involving an 18-story steel frame, a steel pedestrian bridge, and an experimental study, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves more accurate parameter estimates with substantially reduced computational cost than conventional MCMC.

title: Quantum Annealing approaches for Minimal Cut Set identification in fault trees
abstract: The identification of Minimal Cut Sets (MCS) in Fault Trees (FT) is central to Probabilistic Safety Assessment (PSA) but remains computationally challenging. While gate-based quantum algorithms have been explored, Quantum Annealing (QA) has not yet been applied to this industrial use case. This work investigates the application of QA to MCS identification by modeling the FT as a boolean function and implementing three existing SAT to Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) encoding strategies. We evaluate these encodings using generated 3-SAT instances as well as realistic FT benchmarks, and conduct experiments on a simulated annealer and two D-Wave architectures. Our results show that the encoding with reusable auxiliary variables is the most efficient in terms of qubit requirements and embedding scalability. In addition, the Zephyr architecture provides improved embeddability compared to Pegasus, reflected in reduced chain break occurrences and better performance on larger instances. Across these experiments, QA demonstrates the ability to sample diverse valid solutions, making it suitable for exploring the solution space of MCS problems. However, its performance remains limited by hardware constraints and the maximum number of possible shots, which prevent exhaustive identification of all solutions in larger instances.

title: A novel resilience evaluation and enhancement strategy of an interdependent transportation-power distribution system for low-altitude intelligent networks
Credible long-term degradation prediction for proton exchange membrane fuel cell: A physics-informed neural network with conformal prediction approach
abstract: The insufficient durability of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) hinders their commercialization, making accurate long-term prognosis essential. However, existing methods struggle to balance physical interpretability, accuracy, and uncertainty quantification. This paper proposes a novel framework, Physics-Informed Neural Network with Conformal Prediction (PINNCP). First, to address black-box limitations, we develop a gray-box modeling paradigm that integrates physical mechanisms with data. Instead of directly fitting voltage curves, a neural network adaptively learns the meta-parameters of a generalized power-law model. By embedding electrochemical equations into the loss function, the method accurately inverts and decouples key internal physical states without parameter labels. Second, to quantify risks, a physics-informed calibrated conformal prediction strategy is introduced. By calibrating nonconformity scores with physical constraints, it generates prediction intervals with strict statistical guarantees and physical consistency. Extensive validation under static, quasi-dynamic, and dynamic conditions demonstrates that PINNCP accurately predicts long-term voltage degradation trajectories and provides high-quality confidence intervals. Furthermore, by leveraging extracted physical parameters, the method enables degradation prediction transfer across same-type PEMFCs, significantly enhancing practical applicability.

title: Provably near-optimal adaptive topology engineering: Efficient resilience enhancement via trimmed tree intelligence in large-scale critical networks
Temporal fusion multi-layer perceptron enhanced by time-lag-enhanced multidimensional wavelet convolution for remaining useful life prediction
Mechanism-driven resilience modeling and assessment of power system under high-power microwave disturbances
Maintenance modelling methods for industrial systems
Systemic resilience of megacities against respiratory epidemics: A multi-scale coupled framework
Multi-ship collision risk assessment based on multi-criteria evaluation strategy
Multi-layer Bayesian inference of common cause failure probability based on the mixed shock model
A novel data-driven quantitative resilience evaluation method for large-scale systems
abstract: To address disaster-induced damages to systems, resilience theory offers a broader and more practical alternative to traditional risk theory. However, resilience evaluation for large-scale systems faces challenges such as massive data and complex disaster scenarios. This paper proposes a data-driven framework for large-scale system resilience evaluation. First, a standardized dataset structure is defined, and a disaster process recognition method based on metric learning is developed. Second, probabilistic functions linking disaster processes to system performance are established as resilience indicators. Third, a data reduction framework is introduced to mitigate issues of excessive data volume and redundant features by reducing both features and attribute values, thus improving recognition accuracy and reducing storage requirements. Finally, case studies on wind power installations under extreme cold and typhoon threats in two regions of China are conducted. Results show that the average deviation between resilience evaluations based on reduced data and full data is within 5%, while data storage is reduced by 35.8%. This provides data-driven decision support for wind farm managers and alleviates challenges posed by large data volumes.

title: State estimation in smart grids with Gated Recurrent Unit-Kalman Filter Network for Global Positioning System spoofing attack detection and correction
Extending the robustness analysis of uncertain minimum spanning trees via upper set tolerances
abstract: Catastrophic disruptions—natural disasters, cyberattacks, and cascading failures—routinely compromise critical infrastructure networks, where even small simultaneous deteriorations across multiple links can rapidly render optimal spanning trees suboptimal. Classical single-edge tolerance analysis fails to capture such coordinated risk escalations. This paper introduces a new uncertainty-theory-based framework that extends single tolerances to set tolerances : the upper set tolerance (UST) quantifies the maximum total risk increase (distributed arbitrarily across a set of edges) that preserves the optimality of the current minimum spanning tree, while the dual upper set tolerance (DUST) identifies the minimal total increase sufficient to destroy it. We derive exact polynomial-time computation for DUST and tight polynomial-time bounds for UST, eliminating the need for repeated re-optimization. Applied to transportation and infrastructure networks under deep uncertainty, these metrics enable planners to identify critical edge groups, quantify systemic vulnerability, and design more resilient topologies. The framework bridges a long-standing gap between classical sensitivity analysis and modern belief-based uncertainty modeling in reliability engineering.

title: Physics-informed deep surrogate demand modeling for framed core-tube structures under seismic loadings
abstract: Nonlinear time-history analysis of high-rise framed core-tube structures is computationally intensive, particularly when repeated simulations are required for seismic performance evaluation. This study develops a physics-informed deep surrogate framework for rapid prediction of multi-component nonlinear seismic demands. A parameterized family of structural models is generated within practical geometric and material ranges, and nonlinear bidirectional analyses under 500 ground motions are conducted to construct a comprehensive training dataset. Four engineering demand parameters—inter-story drift, top displacement, top acceleration, and base shear—are predicted in a sequence-to-sequence manner. The influence of temporal sequence length on predictive performance and convergence behavior is systematically examined. The optimal configuration achieves test-set coefficients of determination exceeding 0.93–0.95 across all response components. To enhance physical consistency, a hybrid loss formulation incorporating aggregate constraints on peak response, energy balance, and Arias intensity is introduced. While global statistical accuracy remains comparable to purely data-driven models, the physics-informed formulation reduces physically meaningful errors and improves training stability. Once trained, the surrogate enables millisecond-level inference, offering substantial computational savings relative to nonlinear finite-element simulations within the defined structural and seismic parameter domains, and provides a computational basis for future fragility- and reliability-oriented applications.

title: A causality-enhanced network framework for analyzing and governing systemic risk in air traffic control
